body: Coach Tyler welcomed Jonathan Taylor this week with a full tour of the facility. It took four hours, because Coach stopped at every locker to explain who used to be in it. Brock Bowers’ old locker now has a small framed photo and a candle. In my day, you traded a man and never spoke his name again. Coach spoke it eleven times.

Taylor and rookie Jonah Coleman ran the old-fashioned drills, the kind I respect: tire runs, a blocking sled and a man with a whistle. Coleman hit the sled so hard it moved a full yard, and as a reward Coach let him pick the warm-up music. He picked something with a synthesizer, so Coach played the trombone tape instead. Good man, Coach. Newcomers Juwan Johnson and Joe Milton were issued helmets with no logos, which is how it ought to be.

Ladd McConkey (back, questionable) ran the tire drill off to the side at half speed. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Zonovan Knight (concussion), both out, sat with Jeremiyah Love, Terrance Ferguson and Jacory Croskey-Merritt, all on injured reserve, on what the players now call the bench of broken toys. They heckled the tour. I joined them.
reports.headline: Coach Tyler gives Jonathan Taylor a facility tour, and it takes four hours

quote.text: And this is where Brock used to tape his ankles.

body: Hey guys, welcome back to the channel! Today’s vlog is a little different, because Coach Collin did not leave the tunnel. Like, at all. He set up at the locker room door, planted a claymore at the 20-yard line (it’s a prop, relax) and crouched behind a Gatorade cooler staring at it for two straight hours. Nobody went near the 20. The whole practice happened between the 21 and the end zone. Smash that like button!

Meanwhile, the waiver wire kept walking in. Mike Gesicki, Michael Mayer, Isaiah Davis, Chimere Dike and kicker Cairo Santos all showed up this week and had to introduce themselves to each other, because Coach was still at the door. Justice Hill ran the welcome tour wearing a sash that said “Breakout.” Jahmyr Gibbs and Jake Bates ran the same fake punt eleven times, yelling “COACH, YOU CAN COME OUT NOW.” He did not come out.
Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring, injured reserve) watched from the side field and was the only person allowed near Coach, since he was already hurt. Link in bio!
reports.headline: Vlog: Coach Collin runs practice from the tunnel, plants a claymore and does not blink for two hours

quote.text: I’m holding this angle.

body: PEOPLE. PEOPLE. Coach seanwavy showed up to his first practice as the No. 1 seed carrying a gold throne and set it down on the 50-yard line. Then he announced that the fog machine is retired with full honors. It has its own locker now. It has a nameplate. I teared up.

The new arrivals, Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams, got the welcome treatment: they carried the throne from drill to drill while the speakers played a boxing ring announcer’s intro on loop. Kenneth Walker III and CeeDee Lamb ran the “victory lap” drill, which is one lap, very slowly, waving. CeeDee waved at the parking lot. The parking lot waved back. ABSOLUTE SCENES.
Brandon Aiyuk (knee) signed his paperwork on the side field and got the best seat in the house: the throne. Coach made him get up after four minutes.
reports.headline: Coach seanwavy puts a gold throne on the 50 and makes the new guys carry it

quote.text: It’s a Tuesday. Why is there a ring announcer?

body: Name’s Rocco Kowalski, 31 years in the trades. They sent me to cover this outfit because the last reporter showed up in a tiara. Good call. Coach Hogies runs practice like a job site: whistle at 6:58, coffee break at nine sharp, and the whole crew built a new goalpost by hand before lunch. Measured twice, cut once. Level. Plumb. I’ve seen worse work from guys charging triple.

Dak Prescott and Chris Olave ran routes around the sawhorses, and every receiver had to read a tape measure out loud on the way back to the huddle. Backup quarterback Tyler Shough threw the best balls of the morning and got a handshake and a cold one after work. On this crew, that’s a promotion. New guys Josh Jacobs and George Pickens got their tool belts and steel toes on day one.

Light duty on the side field: Jacobs (finger), Pickens (hamstring), David Montgomery (groin) and Carnell Tate (shoulder), all out, sanded two-by-fours, and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, injured reserve) ran the time sheet. At four o’clock everybody clocked out and headed to the bar. First round was on Coach. Good man.
reports.headline: Coach Hogies runs a tight job site: whistle at 6:58, coffee at nine, new goalpost by lunch

quote.text: Measure twice, cut once, block your man.

body: Practice was open today, which is the most suspicious thing that has happened all season. An open practice means they WANT me to see something, so I watched everything. C.J. Stroud threw for two hours straight and never once looked at the sideline. A man with nothing to hide looks at the sideline. Coach Tyriese had the smooth jazz on again, louder this time, which is exactly how you cover the sound of a paper shredder.

Then I saw it. Tank Dell, a bench player, was running with the first team. Nobody announced it. Nobody explained it. When I asked, a team spokesman said, “He’s been on the roster all year.” Has he? Has he, though? The corkboard has a new section labeled DELL, with four strings and a question mark I drew so hard it tore the paper. Tee Higgins was spotted winking again. Same wink, different angle.

Mike Evans (Achilles) and DeVonta Smith (hamstring), both listed out, did their rehab off to the side behind a portable curtain. A curtain. Davante Adams (hamstring, injured reserve) was there too. Or someone wearing his jersey was.
reports.headline: Tank Dell is practicing with the starters. Nobody will say why. I have theories.

quote.text: It’s an open practice. You can just walk in. Please stop crawling.

body: After weeks in the parking lot, I finally got inside. I put on a jersey, grabbed a duffel bag and walked in behind this week’s free-agent signings, Samaje Perine and Demarcus Robinson. Nobody stopped me. Nobody even looked up. The congregation had bigger problems: the Trade God hasn’t made a trade in almost three weeks.

Coach Zach paced the sideline, refreshing the trade block on two phones while the speakers played a slowed-down Sleeper notification sound on loop. Every time it chimed, the whole roster froze. Bijan Robinson scored on every rep without anyone noticing, which the followers called “a sign.” Perine was handed a playbook and told not to get attached to it.

Luther Burden (undisclosed, questionable) did his reps on the side field and kept looking over his shoulder, as players here do. TreVeyon Henderson (illness, out) stayed home again and has been added to the prayer list. I was discovered at the snack table and escorted back to my car.
reports.headline: Undercover: your reporter sneaks in with the free agents and finds the Trade God in withdrawal

quote.text: Someone gets traded tonight. It might be me. It might be the coach.

body: What a Tuesday! Coach Marissa declared it Gratitude Day. Every player wrote a thank-you card to a teammate before stretches, and the speakers played only songs with “sunshine” in the title. There are more of those than you’d think. Seventeen at last count!

Travis Kelce got a card from every player on the roster, plus one from the long snapper’s mom, who was visiting. He read them all aloud. It took most of practice, and nobody minded! Cam Little kicked field goals between cards and made every one. New receiver Darius Cooper got a welcome card the size of a door. Drake Maye wrote “thanks for having me” on his and signed it “your backup, for now :)”.

Patrick Mahomes (elbow, questionable) wrote his cards left-handed off to the side. Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Rashid Shaheed (knee), both out, had their cards read to them softly in the shade. Michael Wilson (neck) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen), on injured reserve, got a fruit basket. Still the best mood in the league!
reports.headline: Marissa’s team holds Gratitude Day, and Travis Kelce gets a thank-you card from everyone

quote.text: Gratitude is free, and so was Darius Cooper!

body: Tuesday rating: four beans out of five, a season high. Coach Tim unveiled a new house blend on the menu board, the Golden-Watson, a double shot so strong the espresso machine had to sit down after the second pour. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson wore aprons and served it to the whole roster themselves. Watson is finally off decaf. The routes were crisp. The foam was crisp. Everything was crisp.

Then a small disaster. Coach Tim brought kicker Spencer Shrader behind the counter to demonstrate the perfect tamp, and Shrader tamped so hard the portafilter flew straight through the uprights. Thirty-nine yards. Good. Coach called it the best kick of the day and docked one bean for the mess.
Jaylen Waddle (head, out) spent the session in the café’s quiet corner with a chamomile and the lights dimmed, which is exactly the right order for that situation. Austin Ekeler wiped down tables.
reports.headline: The Coffey Shop scores a season-high four beans, thanks to the Golden-Watson house blend

quote.text: We’re out of oat milk. We’re out of everything. They drank the whole menu.

body: Today was a landmark session. For the first time this season, Coach Bob turned his attention to defense, specifically the 49ers defense, which he owns. He made the entire offense study it frame by frame. Nobody on this offense will ever play against the 49ers defense in this league. Coach said that is exactly why they must understand it.

Brock Purdy was brought to the front of the room so the group could study his release in slow motion, at one-sixteenth speed, with a cello playing underneath. One throw took eleven minutes to watch. Purdy called it “a lot of looking at myself.” KC Concepcion, who had a big week from the bench, was shown film of the bench itself, so he could understand where he was and why.

Concepcion (leg, questionable) watched the bench film from a bench on the side field, which Coach called “immersive.” Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and MarShawn Lloyd (knee), both out, kept their recliners. Travis Etienne (hamstring, injured reserve) asked for the film to be emailed.
reports.headline: Coach Bob turns film study to his own defense, which no one on the roster will ever face

quote.text: Pause it. Look at the bench. Do you see the bench?

body: Christian McCaffrey reported at seven. Coach Abdo shook his hand, pointed at the field and turned the metal back up. That was orientation.
Jordan Love threw for an hour, and Bucky Irving ran it back every time. Shedeur Sanders, also new, asked where the quarterback room was. He was told “there” and handed a clipboard.

Side field: Lamar Jackson (thumb), Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) and RJ Harvey (knee) are on injured reserve, and Xavier Worthy (hamstring) and A.J. Brown (knee) are out. Nobody talked there either. I went home.
reports.headline: McCaffrey showed up. Love threw. Nobody talked.

quote.text: Louder.

body: Big news from the snack table: Coach Shmoody hired a hibachi chef and set the grill up right on the sideline. Ten out of ten. The onion volcano alone was worth the drive. Football also happened, nearby.

The chef got involved. Every time a receiver ran past, he flipped a shrimp, and you had to catch it in your mouth before you could run your route. Bryce Young threw with a spatula in his back pocket, just in case. Rome Odunze, moving up to No. 1 receiver, caught nine straight and got the first plate. New arrival Quentin Johnston dropped his first shrimp and was sent to the back of the line, which is the hibachi way.

Puka Nacua (knee and toe, injured reserve) caught eleven straight shrimp from a recliner on the side field without ever leaving the chair. The chef called them the best hands he’s ever seen. Kyle Monangai (toe, out) ate beside him, and James Conner (foot, injured reserve) ordered extra yum yum sauce. Ten out of ten again.
reports.headline: Shmoody hires a hibachi chef, and the shrimp-catching drill is born

quote.text: We’re close. I can feel it. Pass the yum yum sauce.

body: WELCOME BACK, FOLKS, to a Tuesday that felt like the final drive of the Super Bowl! Coach Mohammed hauled a full-size game clock onto the field, set it to 2:00 and ran the two-minute drill for the next two hours. Every time the clock hit zero, he reset it and yelled “SAME SITUATION!” The air horns, I can report, have been confiscated by the homeowners’ association.

And here comes Ja’Marr Chase on a go route into three assistants holding pool noodles. He’s got a step, he’s got TWO steps, the ball is in the air… CAUGHT! Chase spiked it, picked it up and spiked it again for the folks in the back row. Coach Mo handed him the game ball. It was the only ball. Practice was delayed eight minutes.

On the side field, Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and Jake Ferguson (knee), both out, called the action from folding chairs into a microphone that wasn’t plugged in. Jonathon Brooks (abdomen) and Alec Pierce (heel), on injured reserve, ran the clock. They ran it badly. It still read 2:00 when I left.
reports.headline: AND THE CROWD GOES WILD: Mo runs the two-minute drill for two straight hours

quote.text: Sir, the HOA has asked me to take the backup air horns too.

body: Coach Tyler gathered the team at midfield for what he called “a short word.” Forty minutes later he was still talking. He said “we sold the Vikings defense because we believe in the Texans” nine times, and once burst into tears over a $35 FAAB balance. In my day a speech was two sentences and a slap on the helmet.

Then came the drill. Players had to run routes while carrying a full cup of coffee, and anyone who spilled had to listen to the trombone tape again. Brock Bowers didn’t spill a drop. New arrival Dylan Sampson spilled on the first step and had to hear the trombone four times before lunch.

Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Zonovan Knight (concussion), both questionable, did the coffee drill off to the side with empty cups. Jeremiyah Love and Pat Bryant, on injured reserve, rode stationary bikes and booed the speech. I joined them.
reports.headline: Coach Tyler’s pregame speech runs 40 minutes and mentions the Vikings defense nine times

quote.text: And that, gentlemen, is why the Texans are a lifestyle.

body: Hey guys, you are NOT going to believe this vlog. Coach Collin canceled practice and threw a full party for Justice Hill’s breakout Thursday night. There was a DJ. There was a balloon arch. There was a cake shaped like Justice Hill’s helmet, and Justice Hill cut it himself while the offensive line sang. Smash that like button!

Coach Collin gave a toast that started “I always believed in this man” and ended “I picked him up for free.” Jahmyr Gibbs ran the only drill of the day: a limbo contest under the end-zone pylons. Gibbs won. Kirk Cousins limbo’d once and said his back was fine. His back did not look fine.
Harold Fannin (groin) and Brian Robinson (hamstring), both questionable, ran the punch bowl off to the side. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg, injured reserve) joined the party on FaceTime. Link in bio!
reports.headline: Vlog: the Justice Hill Breakout Party had a DJ, a cake shaped like his helmet and zero practice

quote.text: I’ve never been a cake before. It’s a lot.
quote.who: Justice Hill, holding a slice of his own helmet

body: FOLKS. FOLKS. Coach seanwavy put BOTH his defenses on the field at once, the Vikings he bought on Thursday and the Bears he’s actually starting, and made the offense run plays against 22 defenders in the fog. Joe Burrow completed a pass anyway. I have never been more alive.

Then Coach gave a speech from on top of the fog machine. He said, and I quote, “We are 6–2 and we will not apologize.” The fog machine overheated halfway through the speech. He kept going. The sprinklers went off. He kept going. Absolute cinema.
Sam Darnold (quadriceps, out) watched from the training room with a towel over the vent. DJ Moore (undisclosed, questionable) ran routes off to the side in a raincoat.
reports.headline: SOMEBODY CALL THE FIRE DEPARTMENT: Sean runs the ‘two defenses, one fog machine’ drill

quote.text: Sir, please get off the fog machine.

body: To honor the arrival of Devin Singletary, purchased at auction for $45 while four rival houses bid in vain, the court introduced a jousting drill. Running backs charged at a tackling dummy dressed as a rival manager while holding foam lances. Chuba Hubbard unseated the dummy three times. The string quartet played a fanfare each time.

Coach Hogies then addressed the court from a balcony. “We are 7–1,” he said, and paused for applause for ninety seconds. He then read the standings a fourth time and dismissed everyone for tea. Trey McBride, the honorary viola, played everyone out.

Christian McCaffrey (calf, questionable) jousted off to the side on a stationary horse. David Montgomery and Carnell Tate, both out, judged from chaises. Jordyn Tyson and Romeo Doubs, on injured reserve, sent their regards from the infirmary.
reports.headline: The court introduces jousting drills to welcome Sir Devin Singletary

quote.text: The dummy has been knighted for its bravery and will be buried with honors.

body: On Tuesday, Mike Evans and DeVonta Smith were listed OUT. On Friday, both are questionable. And today, coincidence of coincidences, Coach Tyriese made every receiver catch passes blindfolded, “so nobody can see the playbook.” Who is trying to see the playbook? I am. I’m trying to see it. I have binoculars.
Coach then gave a speech in a whisper so the media couldn’t hear. I could hear one word: “Higgins.” That’s all I need. The corkboard now has three new strings and a photo of a blindfold.

Evans (Achilles) and Smith (hamstring) did the blindfold drill off to the side with trainers who covered their mouths when they talked. Davante Adams (hamstring surgery) remains on injured reserve, which is exactly what they want you to think.
reports.headline: Tyriese runs blindfolded catching drills ‘so nobody can steal the playbook’

quote.text: The blindfolds are for focus. Please put the binoculars down.
quote.who: A team spokesman, through the fence

body: Still in the parking lot, but I climbed onto my car roof and could see over the wall. The Trade God had the whole roster doing trust falls. Each player fell backwards and the team caught him. When Coach fell, nobody moved, and he landed in a pile of trade offers.

Then Coach Zach gave a speech titled “Every Player Is Temporary.” Bijan Robinson nodded. Luther Burden took notes. Rashee Rice asked if he should unpack his locker. Coach said, “No one should ever unpack.” The new Saints defense quietly kept its bags in the car.

Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs, questionable) did trust falls off to the side onto a mattress. TreVeyon Henderson (illness, questionable) caught people from a respectful distance, which the followers appreciated.
reports.headline: Filed from the parking lot: the Trade God runs a ‘trust fall’ drill with the entire roster

quote.text: Get off the roof. Also, you are not ready.
quote.who: A member of the congregation, at my car window

body: What a Friday! Coach Marissa announced that the team has been practicing football all year and it’s time to practice celebrations instead. They spent 45 minutes on end-zone dances. The worm. The griddy. A seven-man conga line led by kicker Cam Little, fresh off his big Thursday night, who also got a small parade around the field.

Then Coach gave the most uplifting speech I’ve ever heard. “We are 2–6,” she said, “which means six chances to learn and two chances to dance.” Patrick Mahomes, starting this week, wiped away a tear. Drake Maye held the boombox like a proud dad.

Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Garrett Wilson (concussion), Michael Wilson (ribs) and Rashid Shaheed (knee), all questionable, practiced their celebrations from the side, very gently. Tank Bigsby (abdomen, injured reserve) did the wave from a chair. Wonderful!
reports.headline: Marissa’s team practices celebrations for 45 minutes, and Cam Little gets a parade

quote.text: If you can’t score yet, celebrate in advance!

body: Friday rating: three beans out of five, up one. Coach Tim introduced a new drill where players must pour a heart into a latte between every rep. If the heart looks like a blob, you run a lap. Chase Brown ran eleven laps. Matthew Golden poured a perfect fern and was named barista of the week.

Coach then gave a speech about patience. “Two of my waiver orders didn’t come out of the kitchen this week,” he said, referring to Devin Singletary and Dylan Sampson, “but Austin Ekeler walked in off the street, and that’s what this team is about.” Ekeler raised his own mug. The new Lions defense asked for oat milk.
Christian Watson (undisclosed, questionable) did latte art off to the side and moved up to half-caf. Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, who played Thursday, sat in the cold tub with a pour-over.
reports.headline: Tim makes the team run latte-art drills between reps, three beans out of five

quote.text: That fern was better than mine. I’m quitting.

body: Coach Bob reached a new level today. Players watched film of themselves watching film on Tuesday, then broke down what they did wrong while watching. One lineman was caught blinking during a key formation. He apologized to the group.

Then the coach gave a speech using only a laser pointer and diagrams. It lasted an hour and ended with the words “and that is why we always look left.” Jaxon Smith-Njigba gave it a standing ovation. Drake London asked for the slides. Hunter Henry has been released and was not invited.

Dalton Kincaid (chest), Denzel Boston (calf), Alvin Kamara (back), MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), all questionable, watched from the recliners off to the side. Travis Etienne (hamstring, injured reserve) watched from home. Chris Rodriguez, who played Thursday, was excused.
reports.headline: Bob’s new drill: watch film of yourself watching film

quote.text: Look at your eyes here. Your eyes are lying to you.

body: Heavy metal. Coach Abdo put the speaker on the 50 and told everyone to tackle it.
Nobody could. Bucky Irving got closest. Coach gave a speech: “Again.” Jordan Love took every first-team rep.
George Pickens (hamstring) and A.J. Brown (ankle), both questionable, worked on the side. Lamar Jackson (thumb surgery) is on injured reserve. Good practice.
reports.headline: Abdo runs the ‘tackle the speaker’ drill. Speaker wins.

quote.text: Again.

body: I have covered a lot of snack tables, but I have never covered a practice with two giant sewage trucks parked behind the end zone. At 1–7, Coach Shmoody has decided to get ready for the toilet bowl early, and he means it: he also had an Olympic-size swimming pool installed at the 20-yard line, filled with water from the trucks. I am not eating anything near the pool today.

The drill: every player had to dive into the pool, swim to the other end and come out ready to play. Puka Nacua swam it in record time and climbed out holding a football. Bryce Young, the new starting quarterback, did the backstroke and threw a pass from the water. Coach gave a speech from the diving board: “If we’re going down, we’re going down prepared.” The sportsbook still made them 6.5-point favorites this week, which Coach called “a trap.”

Kyle Monangai (toe sprain, questionable) stayed out of the pool and supervised from a lifeguard chair. James Conner (foot, injured reserve) said he would rather not. The snack table, thankfully, was moved to the other side of the building. Nine out of ten.
reports.headline: Shmoody orders two sewage trucks and an Olympic pool to prepare for the toilet bowl

quote.text: I’ve delivered to a lot of places. Never a football field. Never on purpose.

body: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, the drill of the YEAR. Coach Mohammed lined up an assistant with an air horn next to every receiver and blasted it right as the ball arrived. Ja’Marr Chase caught it anyway. Justin Jefferson caught it anyway. Josh Allen threw it while somebody honked at HIM. He completed it. Unreal!

Then Coach gave a pregame speech in the full play-by-play voice. “Mohammed steps to the podium… he looks out at his team… he says… WE’RE NOT DONE YET!” The air horns went off. The fog horn went off. The neighbors went off.

Malik Nabers (undisclosed) and Jake Ferguson (ankle), both questionable, worked off to the side in earmuffs. Jonathon Brooks and Alec Pierce, on injured reserve, asked the training staff to please shut the windows.
reports.headline: TOUCHDOWN AT THE BUZZER: Mo’s new drill is catching passes while the air horns go off in your ear

quote.text: I moved here for the quiet. I want to be very clear about that.

body: Practice opened with Coach Tyler wheeling out a boombox and playing what I can only describe as the saddest trombone solo ever recorded. Thirty years on this beat and I have never seen a warm-up song make the long snapper cry. In my day we warmed up to a whistle and liked it.
Brock Bowers didn’t seem to notice. He ran the same out route eleven times in a row, to the trombone, then asked if anyone had a faster song. Nobody did.

Over on the side field, Jeremiyah Love (ankle, listed out) rode a stationary bike and watched. Cam Skattebo (hamstring, questionable) did light stretching next to him and offered running commentary on the trombone. Coach told them both to keep it down.
reports.headline: Sad trombone on the boombox, and Bowers is running routes to it anyway

quote.text: He says the trombone is ironic. I don’t think it is.

body: Hey guys, welcome back to the practice vlog! Today Coach Collin had the team stretch to a FULL hour of yacht rock. The offensive line was swaying. It was honestly kind of beautiful? Smash that like button.

Jahmyr Gibbs and Tony Pollard turned the ball-security drill into a choreographed routine. I’m not saying it was a dance. I’m saying it had a chorus. Coach let it go because, quote, “the vibes are carrying us.”
Breece Hall (quad, out) was working with trainers off to the side, nodding along to the music. Kirk Cousins was spotted on the bench, which is apparently where he likes it. Link in bio.
reports.headline: Vlog: an hour of yacht rock and Gibbs teaching the line to sway

quote.text: Turn that off. Actually, leave it on. Get my good side.

body: LADIES AND GENTLEMEN. Coach seanwavy installed a fog machine at the end of the tunnel and had every player run out like it was a playoff game. It was a Tuesday walkthrough. I have never been more alive.
Joe Burrow came out of the fog throwing dimes to nobody in particular. Somebody added laser lights halfway through. Jonah Coleman tried to catch a laser. I’m calling it the play of the week.
DJ Moore (questionable, undisclosed) did his work on the side field, where the fog was a little thinner. He waved. The crowd (me) went wild.

body: Practice at the palace opened with Coach Hogies reading the standings aloud to the team. Twice. A string quartet played in the corner. The court finds this entirely appropriate for a team in first place.

Chuba Hubbard was the toast of the court after his weekend, and celebrated by insisting on taking every handoff to the quartet’s tempo. Trey McBride has been made an honorary viola. Kicker Jason Myers was sent to practice field goals at the far end of the grounds, in silence, and the court would prefer not to discuss why.
Christian McCaffrey (calf, questionable) took his reps on the side, with a royal attendant holding a towel. David Montgomery (groin, out) observed from a chaise.

quote.text: First place does not stretch to Top 40. Strings only.

body: Practice today was closed to the media, which is exactly what you’d do if you were hiding something. I did hear music through the fence. Smooth jazz. That is the music of people with secrets. Also: Coach Tyriese changed the team name to No Love in The Land this week. Coincidence? My corkboard says no.
Through a gap in the fence I saw Tee Higgins catching passes one-handed and winking at no one. D’Andre Swift was doing the same drill, also winking. Why are they winking? Who are they winking at?
Mike Evans and DeVonta Smith (both listed out) were off to the side with the trainers. James Cook (questionable, undisclosed) was there too. “Undisclosed.” Sure.
reports.headline: Smooth jazz behind a closed fence, and Higgins knows something

I can also confirm the speakers are playing a motivational podcast at full volume, and the players are nodding along. One of them is taking notes.

Matthew Golden was the bright spot, a nice single-origin pour, running crisp routes and then lining up for a cortado. Jaylen Waddle asked for oat milk, which is how you know he’s ready to start.

cover.dek: The Shidid family civil war continues, the prodigy comes for the master and half the league’s stars are on vacation. Week 6 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.
cover.headline: Brother vs. Brother

games.lineText: (1–4) Baby Abdo - Jackson 🖐️ (+205) vs. (1–4) Shmoody - I Can’t Breathe (−255)
locker: Baby Abdo
Mo got me last week. Shmoody gets me this week? No. Somebody in this family is losing to me, and it’s starting Sunday.
Shmoody
Little bro wants smoke? Big brother strength is different. Two-game win streak starts Sunday. And Oscar, don’t say a word.
games.oscarNote: Oscar said nothing. Oscar has met the family.
games.spreadText: Spread: Shmoody −16.5 | Adjusted Projection: Baby Abdo 104.8 - Shmoody 121.3
story: Last week the oldest brother broke the league record against him. This week Baby Abdo gets the other one.

Nobody in the Shidid family has had a worse October than Abdo. He walked into Week 5 against Mo, ran into a record-setting 196.10 and spent the rest of the night being told to acknowledge his big brother. He has lost three straight, he sits last in the league in points scored at 584.98, and the family dinner table has never felt longer. Revenge on Mo will have to wait. Revenge on Shmoody is available on Sunday.

Shmoody is in no mood to be anybody’s consolation prize. The defending champion finally woke up last week, arrested Sean, burned a Florian Wirtz jersey and won his first game of the season. Now he wants a streak, and he wants to remind little bro that big brother strength is a different kind of strength. Brock Bowers, James Cook and Mike Evans are all rolling. His kicker is on bye, which is the only thing standing between him and a comfortable afternoon.

These two split their meetings last season, one win apiece. This is the rubber match, the family is watching, and one brother leaves Sunday with bragging rights while the other leaves with the dishes.
games.theme: Shidid Family Civil War, Part II
games.title: Baby Abdo vs. Shmoody: Can Little Brother Finally Get Even?

locker: Sean
Kenneth Walker has been located. Case closed. Somebody tell the King his crown is a rental.
Tyriese
Everybody wanted to talk about my draft. Now they want to talk about my crown. I’m gonna be king of the fantasy managers, and Sean’s just a stop on the map.
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −14.0 | Projection: Sean 149.6 - Tyriese 135.4
story: Two managers. Two rivalries that run both ways. And one man who finally has his running back back.

Last week Sean filed a missing person report for Kenneth Walker, got arrested by the defending champion and watched his perfect season leave in the back of a squad car. This week Walker is back from his bye, projected for 21.75, and Sean is projected for the most points in the league at 149.6. The case has been solved. The question is whether the damage is permanent.

Across the field stands King Tyriese, fresh off a 180.34-point raid and two straight wins. The preseason punchline now has Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Derrick Henry on the same ship, and a crown he has no intention of returning. He also beat Sean the only time they met, 104.64 to 100.66 in Week 6 last year.
Sean has the deeper roster. Tyriese has the momentum, the straw hat and a grudge. One of them leaves Sunday as the league’s most dangerous team. The other leaves with a very long Monday.
games.theme: The Case of the Missing Running Back
games.title: Sean vs. Tyriese: Can the King Dethrone the Former King?

watch.text: Fresh off the missing persons list and ready to make up for lost time.
The highest projection on either roster. The King’s first mate needs another 37.

games.lineText: (3–2) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (+310) vs. (4–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (−400)
locker: Tyler
I taught him everything he knows. Unfortunately, I also taught him to check bye weeks.
Hogies
He showed me the way. Now I’m showing him the door. Class is in session, and the teacher doesn’t have a quarterback.
games.spreadText: Spread: Hogies −24.5 | Adjusted Projection: Tyler 114.0 - Hogies 138.6
story: Every master eventually faces the student he created. Tyler taught Hogies how to play this game: how to read a waiver wire, how to work a trade, how to sleep through a 1 p.m. kickoff without checking his phone. On Sunday, the prodigy comes for the man who trained him.

The student has been flawless. Hogies is 4–1, sits at the top of Oscar’s power rankings and has Christian McCaffrey, Chris Olave and Trey McBride ready to go. He has also learned the most important lesson of all: let the other guy talk. Zach found that out the hard way last week.

The master, meanwhile, is riding a three-game winning streak and just declared a national holiday after beating the General. There is one small problem. Jared Goff and the Lions are on bye, and Tyler does not have another quarterback. We are adjusting his projection to 114 on the assumption that the teacher remembers his own first lesson: always have a backup.

The last time they met, the master won 144.80 to 94.02 in Week 11 last year. Hogies has not forgotten. He lists Tyler as a rival, and this is the week he finds out whether the student has truly become the master.
games.title: Hogies vs. Tyler: Can the Student Finally Beat the Teacher?

watch.text: 31.50 last week. The master needs his star pupil of a running back to cover for an empty quarterback slot.
The best player in the matchup and the cornerstone of everything the prodigy has built.

games.lineText: (3–2) Tim - The Coffey Shop (+135) vs. (4–1) Sgt. Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−160)
locker: Tim
I got married, dropped 160, and I’m still the underdog? Fine. Coffee’s on me after.
Sgt. Bob
One loss. The army has been retrained. The honeymoon ends at 1300 hours.
games.spreadText: Spread: Sgt. Bob −8.0 | Projection: Tim 132.9 - Sgt. Bob 140.8
story: One week ago Tim got married and dropped 160.94 on Marissa. One week ago Sgt. Bob lost his first battle of the season. Both men arrive at Week 6 with something to prove.

The General has scored more points than anyone in the league, 736.30 through five weeks, and he treats every Sunday like a military operation. Losing to Tyler stung. The troops have reportedly been running drills ever since, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Kyren Williams and Brock Purdy are all projected for 21 or more.

Tim is still on his honeymoon. Christian Watson and Parker Washington combined for 62.70 points last week, and the Coffey Shop has won three of its last four. Tim lists Bob as a rival. These two have never played, which means the first shot of this war is fired on Sunday.
Bob is the favourite for a reason. But the General learned last week that his army can be beaten, and Tim has a way of surprising people on big weekends.
games.title: Tim vs. Sgt. Bob: Can the Newlywed Ambush the General?

watch.text: 32.30 at the wedding. The groom needs his best man again.
The General’s most decorated soldier and the top projected player on the field.

games.lineText: (1–4) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (+105) vs. (1–4) Mo - Beazy (−125)
locker: Marissa
Everyone’s been talking about Mo’s 196. I’d like to talk about 2–4.
Mo
Chase and Jefferson are on vacation. I’m not. Somebody tell the league the record was a warm-up.
games.spreadText: Spread: Mo −2.5 | Adjusted Projection: Marissa 125.1 - Mo 127.8
story: Last week Mo set the league record with 196.10 and demanded the entire league acknowledge him. This week Ja’Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are both on bye.

That is the problem with being the scariest 1–4 team in history: sometimes your scariest players take the week off. Mo still has Josh Allen, the top projected player in the game at 24.87, and enough depth to field a respectable lineup. Respectable is not 196.

Marissa scored 137.34 last week and lost anyway, then watched Mo post the best score the league has ever seen. She now has Drake Maye and Patrick Mahomes on the same roster and one quarterback slot to put them in. She also beat Mo the last time they met, 161.62 to 112.54 in Week 5 last year.
Two 1–4 teams. One gets to start climbing. The other gets to start explaining.
games.title: Marissa vs. Mo: Can the Record Breaker Do It Without His Stars?

watch.text: 39.46 last week. If he does it again, the spa can finally close.
With Chase and Jefferson on vacation, the record breaker needs his quarterback to carry the house.

games.lineText: (2–3) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+750) vs. (3–2) Zach - Trade God (−1300)
locker: Collin
My lawyer advised me not to comment. My lawyer is also my waiver claim.
Zach
I’m not saying anything until Monday night. Okay, one thing. It’s gonna feel good.
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −41.0 | Projection: Collin 104.2 - Zach 145.4
story: The last time Zach felt good about a matchup, he said so at 1 p.m. and lost at midnight. He has now lost two straight, and the clown makeup has barely come off.

Lucky for the Trade God, he has drawn the friendliest spot of the week. Collin is without Jahmyr Gibbs, who is on bye, and the waiver wire he sued last week has not settled out of court. His lineup projects for 104.2, the lowest in the league.

Zach, meanwhile, has Bijan Robinson projected for 25.43 and a roster built from the Kittle heist. These two list each other as rivals and have never met. On paper it is the biggest mismatch of the week, which is exactly when Zach is most dangerous to himself.
The line is 41 points. The only thing that can beat Zach on Sunday is Zach on Sunday afternoon.
games.title: Collin vs. Zach: Can the Trade God Stop Talking Until Monday?

watch.text: Back on Collin’s roster after a round trip through Tyler’s. He needs to play like a reunion tour.
The best running back projection of the week, and a man who never celebrates early.

cover.dek: Two blockbusters in twelve hours, the last Shidid showdown and a Mo with no quarterback. Week 7 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.
cover.headline: Fallout

games.lineText: (1–5) Shmoody - I Can’t Breathe (−405) vs. (2–4) Mo - Beazy (+310)
locker: Shmoody
I’ve been losing by a touchdown for a month. That ends Sunday. Mo, start whoever you want. It won’t matter.
Mo
Abdo got the record. Marissa got the warning. Shmoody gets the family finale. Somebody find me a quarterback.
games.oscarNote: Oscar is picking Mo on the assumption that he finds a quarterback. If he doesn’t, Oscar was never here.
games.spreadText: Spread: Shmoody −25.0 | Adjusted Projection: Shmoody 114.5 - Mo 116.0 (before Mo finds a quarterback)
story: Three brothers, three weeks, three games. Mo beat Baby Abdo in Week 5. Baby Abdo beat Shmoody in Week 6. Now the oldest and the middle brother settle the last piece of the family round robin, and somebody leaves with the dishes for good.

Shmoody is the defending champion, and he is 1–5. He has lost three games by less than a touchdown, and the latest came against his little brother, by 5.30 points, with 47.60 sitting on his bench. One more loss and a 1–6 record will make him a full-time spectator. Brock Bowers is still rolling, but James Cook and Mike Evans both project zero this week.

Mo is 2–4 and, by his own account, the scariest 2–4 team in history. He set the league record with 196.10 against Baby Abdo. He then beat Marissa without Ja’Marr Chase or Justin Jefferson. This week he has the opposite problem. Chase and Jefferson are healthy and sitting on his bench, and Josh Allen is on bye, the only quarterback on the roster. The sportsbook has taken his lineup at its word and made him a 25-point underdog.

This is also a fight for the head of the family table. Mo has mentioned the 196.10 at every meal since Week 5 and has reportedly asked for it to be engraved on the gravy boat. Shmoody points out that he is the one with the ring, which he now wears to dinner as a precaution. Baby Abdo is 1–1 against the pair this season and holding a framed box score. He has announced he will root for whoever makes the other one wash up.

If Mo starts his stars and finds a quarterback, this is a coin flip with a family dinner on the line. The last time these two met, Shmoody won 117.44 to 79.30. Mo has not forgotten. Neither has the group chat.
games.theme: Shidid Family Civil War, Part III
games.title: Shmoody vs. Mo: Who Owns the Family Dinner Table?

watch.text: The champion’s most reliable weapon, and the TE1 in the market. With Cook and Evans out of the picture, he has to carry the family name.
The best projection in the game, currently on the bench. Mo’s fate depends on one tap of the lineup screen.

games.lineText: (5–1) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (+200) vs. (4–2) Zach - Trade God (−250)
locker: Sean
I got the quarterback. He got a week of buyer’s remorse. See you Sunday.
Zach
I’m not saying anything until Monday. Okay, one thing. I won both trades.
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −16.0 | Projection: Sean 124.1 - Zach 140.2
story: At 12:08 Thursday morning, Sean and Zach made a trade. Twelve hours later Zach traded half of it away again. On Sunday the two men who started it all meet head to head.

Sean sits at No. 1 in the power rankings with the most points in the league, and he went shopping for a quarterback. He got Joe Burrow, one of the three quarterbacks this league actually values, plus DJ Moore and Zach Charbonnet. He paid with Zay Flowers and Matthew Stafford. Burrow scored 24.60 the last time he played. Moore is on bye.

Zach did not stop at one trade. He kept Flowers until lunchtime, then sent him to Tyler with Nico Collins and D’Andre Swift for Amon-Ra St. Brown, Aaron Jones and Luther Burden. He now starts Stafford, Bijan Robinson, St. Brown and George Kittle, and projects 140.2, the second-best number of the week.

The personal stakes are worse than the fantasy ones. Sean has spent a week at No. 1 and has started signing his group chat messages “Respectfully, the No. 1 team.” Zach is back at the pulpit with a new sermon, “How I Fleeced Two Men Before Lunch.” Neither man will admit he lost a trade, and only one of them can win on Sunday. The loser has to read the winner’s trade review in the group chat without replying. For Zach, that would be the longest silence of his career.
Last season Zach won this matchup 184.48 to 152.18. Sean has the better record. Zach has the better projection and a fresh set of toys. One of them is about to find out who won the trade.
games.title: Sean vs. Zach: Can the Trade God Beat the Man He Just Traded With?

watch.text: Bought to win weeks like this one. Scored 24.60 in Week 5 for the man he’s now playing against.
His third team in two weeks. Abdo had him, Tyler had him for a week, and now the Trade God has the WR4.

games.lineText: (3–3) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (−765) vs. (2–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+525)
locker: Tyler
Collin and I have done a lot of business. This is the first time I get to collect.
Collin
Everyone keeps telling me Gibbs is on my bench. I know. It’s called strategy.
games.oscarNote: Oscar has assumed Collin will notice Gibbs. Oscar has been wrong about Collin before.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyler −34.5 | Adjusted Projection: Tyler 134.9 - Collin 134.3
story: Tyler and Collin have traded with each other twice in two weeks. In Week 5 Breece Hall went back to Collin, and Tyler took Luther Burden, Aaron Jones and Brian Robinson. In Week 6 Tyler sent Robinson back for Aaron Rodgers. Now they finally play each other, and almost nothing they swapped is still where they left it.

Tyler spent last week getting schooled by his own student, scoring a league-low 88.52. He answered by trading Amon-Ra St. Brown, a week after acquiring him, for Zay Flowers, Nico Collins, D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. Burden and Jones went to Zach in the same deal. The new lineup projects 134.9, and three of his starters are less than a day old.

Collin has made seven trades and lost two straight. He picked up Kyler Murray on Wednesday and is starting him over Kirk Cousins, the quarterback he traded Stefon Diggs for. Jahmyr Gibbs, the RB1, is on his bench. So are A.J. Brown and Breece Hall.

Off the field, this is a relationship built on paperwork. Tyler and Collin have swapped so many players that their rosters should share a group chat, and Breece Hall has reportedly asked whose house he’s spending Sunday at. Tyler says he won every deal. Collin says he can’t remember the deals, which explains his bench. On Sunday they finally stop negotiating and start keeping score, and neither one is allowed to offer a trade to undo it.

That is why the line looks ridiculous. As set, Collin projects 100.3 and the book makes him a 34.5-point underdog. Start Gibbs, Brown and Hall, and he projects 134.3, a dead heat. The most important manager in this game is Collin’s lineup screen.
games.title: Tyler vs. Collin: Can the Old Trade Partners Settle the Account?

watch.text: His third team in twelve hours. Sean to Zach to Tyler, and he hasn’t had time to unpack.
The highest projection in the league, currently on the bench. Collin’s season may depend on noticing.

games.lineText: (5–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (+170) vs. (4–2) Tim - The Coffey Shop (−210)
locker: Hogies
Tuition is due Sunday. Tim, I accept Venmo.
Tim
Married life is undefeated. The academy is about to have its first dropout.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tim −13.0 | Adjusted Projection: Hogies 126.2 - Tim 132.0
story: One of them just opened a fantasy football academy. The other just got married and has not lost since.

Hogies is 5–1 and fresh off a 45-point lesson to the man who taught him the game. Enrollment at the academy is open. His lineup is a little less polished than his lectures, though. David Montgomery sits in a FLEX spot with a zero projection, and Tyler Shough is putting up points on his bench again.

Tim is 4–2 with two straight wins. He dropped 160.94 on Marissa the week of his wedding and then ambushed Sgt. Bob. Bo Nix, Ashton Jeanty, Chase Brown and Christian Watson give him one of the deepest lineups in the league, and the book has him favored by 13.

This is a clash of lifestyles. Hogies wants to talk about process: waiver theory, bye-week planning and a syllabus he has not shown anyone. Tim wants to talk about his wedding, and the wedding has been worth 286.38 points in two weeks. Hogies has offered Tim a place at the academy. Tim has offered Hogies a slice of leftover wedding cake. Only one of those offers is still fresh.
These two have never met. Somebody’s honeymoon or somebody’s semester ends on Sunday.
games.title: Hogies vs. Tim: Can the Academy Survive the Newlywed?

watch.text: The headmaster’s best student. Hogies needs a big day from him to cover the hole at FLEX.
118.80 points this season, more than any other player on Tim’s roster. The best wedding gift Tim has received.

games.lineText: (3–3) Tyriese - Puka Nacua, 50% off (−185) vs. (2–4) Baby Abdo - Jackson 🖐️ (+155)
locker: Tyriese
Henry owes me 75 points and an apology. He can start paying Sunday.
Baby Abdo
I beat my brother. I can beat a man who invoices running backs.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyriese −10.5 | Projection: Tyriese 133.9 - Baby Abdo 123.4
story: Baby Abdo is coming off the biggest win of his season. Tyriese is coming off an invoice to Baltimore.

Abdo won the family rubber match last week, leads Shmoody 2–1 all time and has reportedly framed the box score for family dinner. He is also still living off the Week 6 deal that sent Amon-Ra St. Brown to Tyler. Bucky Irving, George Pickens, Jameson Williams and DK Metcalf all start for him this week. Lamar Jackson leads the way at quarterback.

Tyriese is 3–3 and holding a playoff spot. Derrick Henry gave him 5.00 points in Week 6, and Davante Adams wasn’t much better. Stefon Diggs, his prize from the Kirk Cousins trade, projects zero this week. Puka Nacua is still Puka Nacua, though, and the book makes Tyriese a 10.5-point favorite.

These two have spent the week sending paperwork. Tyriese has invoiced Baltimore for 75.72 bench points, and Abdo has mailed framed copies of his box score to every member of his family. Tyriese says the win over Shmoody was a family matter and doesn’t count. Abdo says a man who bills his own running back is in no position to judge. The loser has to write the winner a receipt.
Last season Abdo won this matchup 131.24 to 128.54. Expect it to be just as close.
games.title: Tyriese vs. Baby Abdo: Can the Spoils of the Amon-Ra Trade Pay Off?

watch.text: The best projection in the game and the reason his team name is still accurate.
One of the three quarterbacks this league respects. If little brother wins two straight, Lamar is why.

games.lineText: (1–5) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (+220) vs. (4–2) Sgt. Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−275)
locker: Marissa
I beat Bob last year. I’ll beat him again. Somebody just tell me who my kicker is.
Sgt. Bob
The tribunal has concluded. The army marches at 1300 hours. Prisoners will not be taken.
games.spreadText: Spread: Sgt. Bob −18.0 | Projection: Marissa 115.2 - Sgt. Bob 133.0
story: Sgt. Bob has lost two straight and convened a war tribunal. Marissa has had more points scored against her than anyone in the league. Both of them need Sunday.

The General went from the top of the standings to two straight losses, and he has confined MarShawn Lloyd and Denzel Boston to barracks pending investigation. Boston is starting again anyway. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Kyren Williams and Brock Purdy give him a 133.0 projection, and the book has him favored by 18.

Marissa is 1–5. She did plenty right last week and still ran into Mo. Drake Maye is projected for 21.58, but her kicker, Cam Little, is on bye and has a zero next to his name. She will need a new one before Sunday.

This is a grudge with a military file. The General has never forgotten last season’s 138.60 to 105.32 loss, and it is reportedly pinned to his war room wall next to a photo of Marissa labelled “Enemy Combatant No. 1.” Marissa insists she barely remembers the game. That, the General says, is exactly what an enemy combatant would say.
Marissa has the history. The General has the projection. Sunday decides which one goes in the tribunal’s official record.
games.title: Marissa vs. Sgt. Bob: Can the General Win a Battle?

watch.text: The best quarterback projection in this game. If the upset happens, it starts here.
The highest projection in the matchup and 164.86 points this season. The General’s most decorated soldier.

cover.dek: Twelve teams, one battlefield. The three-team trade debuts, Hogies and Bob fight for first, Tyler faces his old players and two teams claw their way out of the Toilet Bowl. Week 8 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.
cover.headline: The League Is at War

games.lineText: (5–2) Zach - Trade God (−130) vs. (3–4) Abdo - Beat the case (+110)
locker: Zach
I collect players. Abdo gave one away. Sunday I'll explain why that was a mistake.
Abdo
Amon-Ra knows what he did. Mo set the record against me. Shmoody lost to me. Zach is next.
games.oscarNote: Oscar is picking against the fans and siding with the man who has Bijan. If Amon-Ra sits, Oscar reserves the right to deny he ever said so.
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −3.5 | Total: 254 | Projection: Zach 128.9 - Abdo 125.2
story: Two weeks ago, Abdo traded Amon-Ra St. Brown to Tyler. Tyler flipped him to Zach a week later. On Sunday, Abdo finally sees him again, wearing the wrong jersey. Amon-Ra is questionable, and Abdo is hoping it stays that way.

Zach is 5–2 and has won his last two, including Sean's profile picture. His playoff odds are 94%. The Trade God has made more deals than anyone except Tyler, and most of them have worked. Bijan Robinson is projected for 21, Amon-Ra and Luther Burden, both from the Tyler blockbuster, give him a pair of starting receivers, and Dallas Goedert holds down tight end. Since Zach puts a deal together every week, the lineup will probably look different again by Sunday.

Abdo is 3–4, and his playoff odds are 15%. He has won two straight and has been building all season: Bucky Irving, George Pickens and DK Metcalf from Tyler, and A.J. Brown last night for Jameson Williams. Omar Cooper Jr. is averaging 22.5 a game. Lamar Jackson is questionable, but Jordan Love is on the bench in case the baby needs a babysitter. A loss puts him at 3–5, and at that point the playoffs are mostly a rumor.
The last two times these two met, they split. Zach won 138.84–106.62 in Week 2 last year, and Abdo got him back 124.24–110.04 in Week 13. The fans like Abdo 4–1. The sportsbook doesn't.
games.title: Zach vs. Baby Abdo: Can Abdo Beat His Old Amon-Ra?

watch.text: The best projection in the game and the reason the Trade God is favored.
Questionable. If he plays, the baby has a chance. If he doesn't, Jordan Love babysits.

games.lineText: (6–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (+180) vs. (5–2) Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−220)
locker: Hogies
Byes don't scare me. I've been winning with backups all year. Bob's points don't count on the standings page.
Bob
Enjoy the view from first place, Hogies. It's about to be a lot shorter.
games.oscarNote: First place is a lovely address, but Hogies is only renting it. Bob has the lease, the furniture and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
games.spreadText: Spread: Bob −14 | Total: 212.5 | Adjusted Projection: Bob 128.7 - Hogies 114 (with Hogies' bye-week replacements)
story: First place is on the line. Hogies is alone at the top at 6–1 and has won three straight. Bob is a game back at 5–2. He has also scored 982 points to Hogies' 980, so the man in first is chasing the man with the better team on paper. If Hogies wins, he goes to 7–1 and opens up a two-game lead. If Bob wins, they're both 6–2, and Bob takes first on points.

Hogies has picked a bad week to lose half his lineup to byes. Christian McCaffrey, Chris Olave, Jaylin Noel and Jordan Watkins all have the week off, and so do most of the players on his bench. He'll be shopping on the waiver wire by Sunday. What he has left is good, though. Dak Prescott is projected for 22.7, Trey McBride is the best tight end in the league that doesn't belong to Tyler, and Chuba Hubbard has quietly averaged 18 a game. The student has become a teacher in the standings, but this week he's a substitute teacher.

Bob has Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is averaging 28 points a game and is the most dangerous receiver in the league. Kyren Williams adds 19.6 a game, and Drake London and Denzel Boston fill out a receiving room that would make most teams jealous. The only question mark is at quarterback, where Malik Willis is starting and hasn't played a down for him yet.
Bob has owned this matchup. He beat Hogies 166.94–91.14 in Week 6 last year and won again in Week 15, 141.68–132.48. The fans like Bob 4–1.
games.title: Hogies vs. Sgt. Bob: Who Owns First Place?

watch.text: With four starters on bye, the tight end has to play like a wide receiver and a running back at once.
28 points a game. The most dangerous receiver in the league, and Hogies has nobody to match him.

games.lineText: (3–4) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (+405) vs. (5–2) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−555)
locker: Tyler
Sean doesn't have a team. He has my old team. I know every one of those guys' weaknesses.
Sean
Thanks for CeeDee. Thanks for Walker. Thanks in advance for the win.
games.oscarNote: Tyler built a better team this week, but Sean built his out of Tyler's old one. Oscar is sad to report that the original still beats the remake.
games.spreadText: Spread: Sean −30 | Total: 250.5 | Adjusted Projection: Sean 140.9 - Tyler 122.4 (line set before the three-team trade)
story: Sean's team is named after CeeDee Lamb, and Tyler is the one who traded him there. Before Week 1, Tyler sent CeeDee to Sean for Kenneth Walker. A week later, he sent Walker to Sean too. On Sunday, Tyler faces the two best players he's ever traded away, both wearing the same jersey. Walker is averaging 24.6 a game and CeeDee 22.2. Zay Flowers went to Sean and came back, and Joe Burrow arrived from Zach. Half of Sean's team has a receipt with Tyler's name on it.

Tyler is 3–4, has lost two straight and has lost on the final play three times this season. His playoff odds were 25% before Tuesday night, when he made the first three-team trade in league history to land Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams. With Williams, Flowers and Bowers, Tyler finally has the firepower to match Sean's big three. Jared Goff runs the offense, and Makai Lemon and Antonio Williams are his flex plays. The questions are Ladd McConkey and Jeremiyah Love, who are both questionable. The sportsbook set this line before the trade, which is why it reads like an insult.

Sean has scored 998 points, the most in the league, and he's 5–2 even after losing his profile picture to Zach last week. His big three are Walker, CeeDee and Joe Burrow, and Jonathan Taylor makes them a big four. His only soft spots are DJ Moore and Zach Charbonnet, who are both questionable.
Tyler has the history on his side. He beat Sean twice last year, 154.08–98.84 in Week 1 and 123.22–99.94 in Week 12. The fans like Sean 4–1.
games.title: Tyler vs. Sean: Can Tyler Beat His Old Team?

watch.text: The prize of the three-team trade makes his debut. Tyler needs him to play like the TE1 on day one.
Averaging 24.6 a game since Tyler sent him over. Every point is a reminder.

games.lineText: (3–4) Tyriese - Welcome to Loveland 🫶 (+180) vs. (3–4) Mo - Beazy (−220)
locker: Tyriese
Mo has three stars. I have ten starters. Do the math.
Mo
I set the record without a quarterback. Now I have one. Welcome to Loveland? Welcome to the beast.
games.oscarNote: Depth is a comfort in October, but stars win in November. Mohammed has three, and Tyriese traded his only one away on Tuesday.
games.spreadText: Spread: Mo −14 | Total: 258 | Adjusted Projection: Mo 139.5 - Tyriese 122.6
story: Both are 3–4, and the winner reaches .500. Mohammed holds the sixth playoff spot on points, and Tyriese sits just behind him. A loss doesn't end anyone's season, but it does start the countdown.

Tyriese spent Tuesday night rebuilding his roster. In four trades, he added James Cook, D'Andre Swift, Tee Higgins, Jalen Coker and DeVonta Smith, and briefly Kyler Murray, for about 25 seconds. This is the debut of the new Loveland. Caleb Williams leads it, Cook and Swift share the backfield, and Higgins, Coker and Stefon Diggs make up the receivers. The team runs five deep at receiver and running back. What it doesn't have anymore is Puka Nacua, and on a big week, a superstar wins games that depth can't.

Mohammed has won three straight and is the hottest team in the league. He set the league record with 196.10 against Abdo and has gone 3–0 since. Josh Allen is back from his bye, and Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are both healthy. Both of those receivers came over in trades, and Jefferson came from Tyler. Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are on bye, but his bench covers both spots. At full strength, this might be the most talented team in the league, and he's no longer playing without a quarterback.
Last year, Tyriese beat Mohammed 179.12–130.68 in Week 4. The fans like Mohammed 4–1.
games.title: Tyriese vs. Mo: Can Depth Beat the Beast?

watch.text: His third team in a week. Tyriese gave up Puka to get him, so he'd better feel at home fast.
Back from the bye. Last week Mo had no quarterback; this week he has the best one in the game.

games.lineText: (3–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+165) vs. (4–3) Tim - The Coffey Shop (−200)
locker: Collin
They call me the annoyance of the league. Tim's about to find out why.
Tim
I took Mahomes out of my lineup and got better. Imagine what I'll do to Collin.
games.oscarNote: Collin has the best player on the field and the worst luck in the league. On Sunday, Oscar expects the luck to win.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tim −12 | Total: 264.5 | Adjusted Projection: Tim 139.8 - Collin 118.9
story: This is the new guys' game. Collin took over Jordan's team this year, and Tim took over Ryan's. Neither has had a full season to earn a reputation, and both have spent this one making a name in the trade market. Tim is 4–3 with playoff odds of 74%. Collin is 3–4 at 36%, and a loss would make it feel a lot lower.

Collin has been the league's busiest trader after Tyler, and on Tuesday night he made three more deals. He added Jameson Williams and Josh Downs, plus $63 in FAAB. Last week Jahmyr Gibbs sat on his bench. This week Gibbs starts, and at 28.5 points a game he's the best running back in the league. Kirk Cousins has averaged 18.8 since arriving, Tony Pollard is steady, and Germie Bernard has quietly put up 15.7 a game. Breece Hall is questionable again. Collin has also been unlucky: 975 points have been scored against him, the second-most in the league. He's a better team than his record says.

Tim's best move came in Week 4, when he got Bo Nix and $100 of FAAB for Patrick Mahomes. Since then, he's built a deep, balanced team. Trevor Lawrence is projected for 21.4, Ashton Jeanty and Chase Brown share the backfield, and Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Parker Washington are all averaging more than 15 a game. His one weak spot is at tight end, where Kyle Pitts is averaging 5.7 points a game. Golden and Jaylen Waddle are both questionable.
These two have never played each other. The fans like Tim 4–1.
games.title: Collin vs. Tim: Can the Annoyance Survive the Coffey Shop?

watch.text: 28.5 a game and out of the lineup last week. Collin will not make that mistake twice.
The engine of the Coffey Shop. If he gets going early, Collin's comeback math stops working.

games.lineText: (1–6) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (−220) vs. (1–6) Shmoody - I Can’t Breathe (+180)
locker: Marissa
Everybody keeps scoring 160 on me. Shmoody doesn't have 160 in him.
Shmoody
I'm still the champion. Puka just got here. The basement is for Marissa.
games.oscarNote: The fans believe in the champion and Oscar respects the sentiment. But Marissa has the better lineup, and Shmoody has the better excuses.
games.spreadText: Spread: Marissa −13.5 | Total: 253.5 | Adjusted Projection: Marissa 134.0 - Shmoody 116 (line set before the three-team trade)
story: The two 1–6 teams play for the right to not be alone in last place. The loser falls to 1–7. The winner escapes the basement, at least for a week. Both are down to playoff odds of 2% and 4%, and the sportsbook makes them the top two favorites for the Toilet Bowl.

Last year, Shmoody won the whole league. Now he's 1–6, has lost three games by less than a touchdown, and has had enough of waiting. Over five days, he traded for D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins, then sent them away again to land Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry in the three-team trade. Both debut on Sunday. Geno Smith is averaging 23.5 a game, more than almost any quarterback in the league. The rest of the lineup is the problem: Blake Corum, Rome Odunze and Ja'Kobi Lane aren't scaring anyone. The sportsbook set this line before the trade, so it still prices Shmoody without Puka.

Marissa has scored 807 points, the fewest in the league, and 1,005 have been scored against her, the most. Some of that is her team and some of it is bad luck. Drake Maye has been solid, Tetairoa McMillan is averaging 16.2, and Bhayshul Tuten, her team's namesake, is averaging 14.7. The other half of the name has been the problem: Saquon Barkley is averaging 7.6 a game and is questionable again. She also has Patrick Mahomes sitting on her bench, which is a sentence that should never apply to a 1–6 team.
Last year Marissa beat Shmoody 111.24–106.20 in Week 11. The fans like Shmoody 4–1.
games.title: Marissa vs. Shmoody: Who Gets Off the Bus?

watch.text: He has run in a touchdown two weeks straight. Marissa needs a third.
The prize of the three-team trade debuts. The champion is betting the season on him.

parlay.headline: Twelve legs, three debuts, one golden boy
parlay.intro: One anytime touchdown from every team. Quarterbacks only count if they run one in.
picks: 28.5 points a game and finally back in the lineup. The surest thing on the slip.
The Trade God's one untouchable. Atlanta gives him the ball at the goal line.
Green Bay's goal-line back. Abdo needs a touchdown more than anyone in the Game of the Week.
Bob's touchdown machine near the end zone, and a safer bet than JSN to find paydirt.
With McCaffrey on bye, Hogies' backfield belongs to him.
Day one of the three-team era. Dallas's lead back should get the short ones.
Two touchdowns the last time Oscar picked him. Tyler would prefer he forget how.
Third team in a week, same end zone. Buffalo always finds him there.
Back from the bye and the best running quarterback in the league. Oscar has learned this lesson before.
Oscar missed on him in Week 5. Oscar does not hold grudges, only parlay slips.
Two straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Oscar is going for three.
The champion's new back is 32 years old and has never once been stopped at the 1-yard line.
parlay.sign: Gibbs is the golden leg. Josh Allen is the danger leg, because Oscar's quarterback picks have gone 3-for-6. If all twelve cash, Oscar retires to the countryside.

cover.dek: The league is running out of excuses. Zach and Mo climb the ladder for the Smoke Boy belt, Hogies hunts from first place, Tyriese and Shmoody settle the three-team trade, and Tyler and Abdo fight for their playoff lives. Week 9 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.
cover.headline: The League's Judgment Day

games.lineText: (6–2) Zach - Trade God (−135) vs. (3–5) Mo - Beazy (+110)
locker: Zach
Mo can have the points. I'll take the wins. That's how you get a belt.
Mo
I've scored more than everybody and lost to everybody. Somebody's paying for that Sunday, and it's the Trade God.
games.oscarNote: Luck is a fine thing until it runs out, and Zach has been borrowing it all season. Oscar expects Mo to finally climb high enough to collect the debt, and the belt.
games.spreadText: Spread: Zach −4 | Total: 285.5 | Projection: Zach 144.8 - Mo 140.6
story: The belt hangs over the ring and both men are on the ladder. The Smoke Boy Championship goes to whoever reaches it first, and the 285.5-point total is the highest of the week, so the sportsbook expects fireworks.

Zach is 6–2 and has won three straight, including a 126.28–84.90 win over Baby Abdo last week. His playoff odds are 99%. He's also the luckiest team in the league: only 897.5 points have been scored against him, the fewest of any team. Bijan Robinson leads the league's best backfield with 153 points and is projected for 23.2 this week. Amon-Ra St. Brown has 141 and is questionable. Jayden Daniels is projected for 18.6 at quarterback, and George Kittle is back from his bye at tight end. The Trade God has found a way every week, and the record shows it.

Mo is 3–5, which makes no sense. He has scored 1,125 points, the second-most in the league, and has had the second-most scored against him. Last week he put up 147.66 and still lost to Tyriese's 166.98. No one has been less rewarded for doing more. Josh Allen is projected for 22.4 and ran in a touchdown last week. Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are the best receiver pair on the field, and Malik Nabers is back from his bye too. His playoff odds are still 80%, because the math knows something the standings don't.
The only time these two have met, Mo won 111.90–82.52 in Week 11 last season. The fans like Mo 6–2, the most lopsided vote of the week.
games.title: Zach vs. Mo: Who Climbs the Ladder for the Smoke Boy Championship?

watch.text: 153 points and the league's best backfield. If he finds the end zone, the belt goes to the Trade God.
Ran one in last week. Mo has scored more than almost anyone; Allen is how he finally gets paid for it.

games.lineText: (7–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (−145) vs. (2–6) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (+120)
locker: Hogies
First place, four straight, and the bartenders know my name. Marissa's just another stop on the tour.
Marissa
Everybody's been scoring 160 on me all year. Last week I did it back. Hogies is next.
games.oscarNote: Marissa has the hot hand and two quarterbacks, but Hogies has first place and the habit of winning. Oscar has learned not to bet against a man the bartenders love.
games.spreadText: Spread: Hogies −5.5 | Total: 259 | Projection: Hogies 132.4 - Marissa 126.8
story: Hogies is 7–1, has won four straight and sits two games clear in first. Last week he beat Bob with half his team on bye, four waiver pickups and an empty bench. This week the regulars are back: Christian McCaffrey is questionable but projected for 22.9, Chris Olave returns at 15.4, Dak Prescott is projected for 19.8, and Trey McBride and Chuba Hubbard give him two more steady starters. Behind them, though, the bench is held together with tape. Carnell Tate is out, and Romeo Doubs and Jordyn Tyson are on IR. His playoff odds are 99.9%, so this is about keeping the lead, not making the playoffs.

Marissa is 2–6, but she's coming off her best game of the season. She dropped 166.06 on Shmoody last week. She's also been the unluckiest team in the league: 1,127.54 points have been scored against her, the most of anyone. Drake Maye is projected for 21.0 and has run in a touchdown three weeks straight. Tetairoa McMillan is steady, and Patrick Mahomes is projected for 21.2 on her bench, so she may be the only manager with two starting quarterbacks. The problem is her injury report: Saquon Barkley, Travis Kelce, Garrett Wilson, Michael Wilson and Bhayshul Tuten are all questionable. Her playoff odds are 9%, and every win from here is a must.
These two split last season. Hogies won 103.02–93.86 in Week 3, and Marissa won 111.40–96.58 in Week 14. The fans like Hogies 5–2.
games.title: Hogies vs. Marissa: The Hunt

watch.text: Questionable. If he plays, the hunter has his biggest weapon back.
Three straight weeks with a rushing touchdown. Marissa needs him to keep running.

games.lineText: (4–4) Tyriese - No Love in The Land (−125) vs. (1–7) Team Shmoody (+105)
locker: Tyriese
I gave him Puka and he still can't win. The trade's over, and so is his season.
Shmoody
Ask Tyriese what happened in the quarterfinals last year. I end seasons. Ask him about it Sunday.
games.oscarNote: Shmoody has the brightest star on the field and a champion's memory. Tyriese has five starters for every one of Shmoody's. Oscar expects arithmetic to beat nostalgia.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyriese −3 | Total: 269.5 | Projection: Tyriese 136.2 - Shmoody 133.5
story: Two weeks ago, these two were on opposite ends of the first three-team trade in league history. Tyriese gave up Puka Nacua and Derrick Henry and walked away with five starters. Shmoody went the other way, sending out D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins five days after getting them. On Sunday, the trade plays itself out on the same field, and both sides will finally find out who won it.

So far it's been Tyriese. He's 4–4, and last week his new depth beat Mo 166.98–147.66, one of the best scores of the season. Caleb Williams is projected for 18.5, and Swift and Higgins, both from Shmoody, are each projected for 16.6. James Cook adds 15, and Mike Evans is questionable but could be back from injury, projected for 16.4. His playoff odds are 85%, and this is the kind of game that keeps him there.

Shmoody won the whole league last year. Now he's 1–7, has lost three straight and sits alone in last, with playoff odds of 2%. He does have the best player on the field: Puka Nacua is projected for 23.1. Nico Collins adds 17.8, and Henry is still Henry. Kyler Murray is questionable at quarterback, but Bryce Young is right behind him at 17.1. The team is good enough to win; it just hasn't.

Tyriese beat Shmoody 108.80–90.52 in the regular season last year, but Shmoody got the one that mattered. He knocked Tyriese out of the playoffs 162.40–134.30 in the quarterfinals on his way to the title. The fans like Tyriese 7–1.
games.title: Tyriese vs. Shmoody: Who Claims the Treasure?

watch.text: Traded away by Shmoody twice in five days. This is the revenge game.
The prize of the three-team trade and the best projection on the field.

games.lineText: (4–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+245) vs. (5–3) Bob - Shedeur Stay, Shedeur Go (−305)
locker: Collin
Seventeen points last week, twenty this week. Keep adding points, I'll keep winning.
Bob
Collin got lucky once. I've got JSN and a real quarterback now. Lightning doesn't strike twice.
games.oscarNote: Collin has made a habit of embarrassing the sportsbook, and Oscar admires a good habit. But Bob has the best receiver in the league and finally a quarterback to throw to him. Oscar takes Bob to win, and Collin to cover.
games.spreadText: Spread: Bob −20 | Total: 261 | Projection: Bob 140.5 - Collin 120.6
story: Last week Collin was a 17-point underdog against Tim and won 122.36–95.20. This week the sportsbook has made him a 20-point underdog, apparently to see whether he can do it twice. He's won two straight, he's 4–4, and his playoff odds are a coin flip at 49%.

Collin's case starts and ends with Jahmyr Gibbs. Gibbs has scored 195.8 points this season, and at 25.8 he's the highest-projected player in this game. Kirk Cousins is steady at 17.4, and Jameson Williams and Josh Downs, both from his busy trade night, are in the lineup. Behind them it gets thin, and with 1,070.88 points scored against him, Collin has had to beat good scores all year. He's done it the last two weeks.

Bob is 5–3 with playoff odds of 95%, and he's coming off a 101.90–91.14 loss to Hogies with Malik Willis at quarterback. He's done waiting on that: Brock Purdy is in and projected for 22.2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has scored 219.96 points, the most of any receiver in the league, and is projected for 24. Drake London (19.0) and Kyren Williams (18.7) make it the deepest lineup on the field. Deebo Samuel, Denzel Boston and Alvin Kamara are all questionable, but Bob has enough to cover for them.
These two have never played each other. The fans are split 4–4, so the league isn't as sure as the sportsbook.

Mo is the most dangerous 1–4 manager imaginable: his 704.26 season points and historic 196.10-point Week 5 eruption suggest the record is hiding a genuine threat. Shmoody, Marissa and Baby Abdo need to start stacking victories immediately.

body: Four weeks. Four losses. Four weeks of being called the biggest disappointment in fantasy football. Mo entered Week 5 with the weight of an entire preseason's worth of hype on his shoulders and a record that made him look less like a title contender and more like a man reserving a seat in the Toilet Bowl.
Then his little brother showed up. And apparently, that was all the motivation Mo needed.

In the most outrageous performance the league has ever witnessed, **Mo detonated for 196.10 points**—a new all-time single-week scoring record. Not a narrow escape. Not a lucky Monday-night comeback. An 80.12-point family demolition that turned a rivalry game into a historical document.
Baby Abdo finished with 115.98 points, a total that might have kept him competitive on another Sunday. Against his older brother, it was barely enough to get a seat at the dinner table.

The scene at the Shidid family dinner was reportedly unbearable. Mo climbed onto a chair, lit an enormous celebratory blunt, pointed at his younger brother and delivered the only words anyone would hear for the rest of the night: **“ACKNOWLEDGE ME.”** Abdo, already covered in the metaphorical spaghetti of defeat, could only stare at the scoreboard and wonder how a perfectly ordinary family gathering had become a public execution.

For Mo, this was bigger than finally putting a number in the win column. He came into the season regarded as one of the favorites and spent the first month watching that reputation disintegrate. One record-setting Sunday cannot erase a 1–4 start, but it absolutely changes how opponents will look at his roster. Nobody can dismiss a team capable of dropping nearly 200 points.

For Abdo, the damage goes beyond the standings. He is also 1–4, he just surrendered a league record to his own brother, and his desperate campaign to get Josh Jacobs back has become the family’s second-most-discussed crisis. At this point, the kid may need a trade, a miracle, and a new place to eat Thanksgiving dinner.

body: For four weeks, Sgt. Bob ruled the league like a five-star general who had never heard the word defeat. His troops were organized, his record was spotless, and his undefeated army marched into Week 5 expecting another helpless opponent to surrender.

Unfortunately for Bob, Tyler didn't arrive to negotiate a ceasefire. He arrived with a Manchester City cap, Pep Guardiola on the sideline, and an offense ready to turn a military operation into a demolition site.

Tyler unleashed **163.94 points**, defeating Bob's 121.76 by **42.18 points**. The result delivered Tyler his **third consecutive victory**, pushed his record to 3–2, and handed the previously undefeated general his first loss of the season.

The victory was powered by a three-man offensive air raid. **Bucky Irving erupted for 31.50 points**, **Jared Goff delivered 28.94**, and **George Pickens added 28.00**. Together they scored **88.44 points**—a relentless assault that left Bob's defensive game plan in ruins.

Bob had some soldiers who showed up for duty: **Jaxon Smith-Njigba posted 22.80 points** and **Kyren Williams contributed 19.60**. But the reinforcements never arrived. **Dalton Kincaid scored 3.70**, **Deebo Samuel managed 2.50**, and **Alvin Kamara produced just 2.60**. That trio combined for a miserable **8.80 points** while Tyler's stars were lighting up the scoreboard.

Tyler began the season 0–2 after two agonizing defeats. Three straight wins later, he's 3–2, has just taken down the league's undefeated general, and looks like a contender nobody wants to draw. Bob remains 4–1 and a serious championship threat, but his aura of invincibility is gone. The army can be beaten—and Tyler just published the battle plans.
stories.headline: The General has fallen! Tyler's third straight win ends Bob's perfect season
