body: At 1 p.m. Sunday, Zach decided he had already won. The self-proclaimed Trade God looked at an early lead over Hogies and announced, with the confidence of a man who had apparently never watched a full NFL Sunday: **“It feels good to win.”**
The only issue was that an entire afternoon, Sunday night, and Monday night of football remained. Zach had delivered the victory speech before the game had finished its first act.

By the time the dust settled, Hogies had escaped with a **111.64–106.30 win**. The league had witnessed an extraordinary four-stage transformation: smug confidence, nervous laughter, full clown makeup, and finally silence.

Hogies did not need a record-breaking performance. He needed the right players to step up—and, perhaps more importantly, Zach to keep talking. **Kicker Jason Myers erupted for 23.00 points**, a ridiculous total from a position that rarely gets to be the headline. **Trey McBride added 21.60**, while **Christian McCaffrey supplied 17.30**. Those three alone accounted for **61.90 points**, more than half of Hogies’ final total.

Zach had stars of his own. **Joe Burrow led the team with 24.60**, **D’Andre Swift delivered 17.30**, and **Bijan Robinson contributed 15.80**. But the supporting cast turned the Trade God’s celebration into a funeral procession: **David Montgomery scored 1.10, Carnell Tate 1.60, Romeo Doubs 2.60, TreVeyon Henderson 4.80, and the Steelers defense 1.00**. Five lineup spots produced just **11.10 points combined**.

By Sunday night, Hogies had reached **111.64** while Zach was stranded at **98.50**. Monday offered one last chance at salvation. Zach crept to **106.30**, but finished **5.34 points short**. Hogies moved to 4–1; Zach fell to 3–2 with a second straight defeat and the most replayed premature victory speech in league history.
stories.headline: “It feels good to win!” Zach celebrates early, Hogies gets the last laugh
press: He was celebrating before half the league had even kicked off. I just let him keep talking.

body: Four games into the season, the defending champion looked less like a reigning king and more like a man selling his championship ring on Facebook Marketplace. Shmoody was 0–4, his title defense was collapsing, and the rest of the league was already writing the obituary.
Across the field stood Sean Wavy: inaugural champion, unbeaten at 4–0, and convinced his latest title campaign would be a coronation. Instead, the former king walked into a police sting.

Shmoody finally delivered the performance everyone had been waiting for, hammering Sean **147.78 to 107.32**. A **40.46-point** rout ended Sean’s perfect start and gave the defending champion his first victory. In the Gazette’s official crime-scene reconstruction, Officer Shmoody arrested Sean for fraudulent championship claims and seized the allegedly counterfeit ring as evidence.

The rescue operation had several heroes. **Mike Evans erupted for 26.30 points**, **Jacoby Brissett added 25.28**, **Brock Bowers supplied 23.00**, and **James Cook contributed 22.80**. Those four combined for **97.38 points**, turning a desperate must-win into a public humiliation of the league’s last unbeaten former champion.

Sean did get **27.32 points from Matthew Stafford**, but the supporting cast fell apart. **CeeDee Lamb scored only 2.90**, **Jonathan Taylor managed 11.20**, **Will Shipley posted 8.30**, and the **Cowboys defense finished at minus 2.00**. Kenneth Walker’s bye did not help. When your star receiver barely shows up and your defense actively subtracts points, the undefeated record starts looking very temporary.

The aftermath was every bit as dramatic as the scoreboard. Shmoody reportedly removed his 2025 championship ring from Facebook Marketplace and celebrated by burning a Florian Wirtz jersey. Sean, meanwhile, must explain how a 4–0 juggernaut was dismantled by the one manager everybody had already buried. The defending champion is still only 1–4, but for one glorious week he reminded the league why he wears the crown.
stories.headline: The champion refuses to die! Shmoody arrests Sean and ends his undefeated run

body: They laughed at the draft. They questioned the roster. They said Tyriese had built a fantasy football team that belonged at the bottom of the ocean. Five weeks later, the same manager is standing on the bow of the Going Merry, wearing a straw hat, and shouting to the entire league: **“I’M GONNA BE KING OF THE FANTASY MANAGERS!”**

This was no ordinary win. Tyriese unleashed **180.34 points** against Collin’s 115.20, delivering a **65.14-point beatdown** and moving to 3–2. The preseason punchline has become one of the most explosive teams in the league, and the rest of the managers suddenly have very little to laugh about.
Collin entered the matchup hoping to steady a season that had already been full of frustration. Instead, he ran directly into a pirate ship loaded with touchdowns.

**Puka Nacua led the raid with 37.70 points**, and he had plenty of company. **Davante Adams scored 22.10**, **Derrick Henry supplied 21.00**, **C.J. Stroud delivered 20.94**, and **Sam LaPorta added 19.80**. Even the supporting cast got involved: **Ka’imi Fairbairn kicked in 17.00** and the **Texans defense added 16.00**. It was less a lineup than an entire pirate crew firing cannons at the same target.

Collin had one genuine superstar performance: **Jahmyr Gibbs erupted for 37.70 points**, matching Puka at the top of the individual scoring sheet. **Aaron Rodgers contributed 22.00** and **Braelon Allen delivered 18.60**. But a handful of starters were practically invisible. **Roman Wilson scored 0.00, Tre Harris 3.60, Harold Fannin Jr. 1.40, and T.J. Hockenson 1.70**. Those four combined for just **6.70 points**, wiping out much of Gibbs’s heroic effort.

For Tyriese, this is a second straight win and a full-blown transformation from draft-night joke to championship threat. For Collin, now 2–3, the message is simple: one superstar cannot carry an entire crew when half the ship has fallen overboard.

body: Most people celebrate their wedding weekend with a cake, a first dance, and a few speeches. Tim apparently decided those traditions were not enough. He added a **160.94-point fantasy football explosion** and a win over Marissa, because nothing says newlywed bliss quite like demolishing somebody else’s Sunday.

The Coffey Shop was serving touchdowns all weekend. Tim moved to **3–2** with a **23.60-point victory**, while Marissa dropped to **1–4** despite posting an impressive **137.34**. On most weeks, that is a score worth celebrating. Against the groom, it was just another piece of wedding cake.

The wedding party had plenty of MVPs. **Christian Watson erupted for 32.30 points**, **Parker Washington followed with 30.40**, and kicker **Spencer Shrader supplied a ridiculous 21.00**. Those three alone combined for **83.70 points**. **Trevor Lawrence added 21.74** and **Matthew Golden contributed 20.30**, leaving Marissa chasing a reception hall full of touchdowns.

Marissa did not go quietly. **Drake Maye exploded for 39.46 points**, the biggest individual score in this matchup. **Garrett Wilson added 23.40**, and the **Broncos defense scored 17.00**. **Bhayshul Tuten delivered 11.60** and **Wan’Dale Robinson 11.30**. But **Chris Rodriguez (2.10)**, **Marvin Wilson (7.28)**, and **Mike Gesicki (7.40)** could not keep pace with Tim’s entire wedding party.

Somewhere in South Park, the kids are eating a giant wedding cake marked 160.94 while Cartman screams about a Starbucks burning down. That image pretty much sums up Marissa’s season: enough offense to make things interesting, followed by something catching fire at the worst possible moment.

body: In the Shidid family, Baby Abdo has always sat at the end of the table. Mo is the oldest. Shmoody is the one with the ring, the 2025 champion who beat Tyler 173.30 to 107.30 in the final. Abdo is the one they tell to clear the plates.

That pecking order took a beating last week. Mo dropped a league-record **196.10** on Abdo and spent the night demanding to be acknowledged. Abdo went into Week 6 on a three-game losing streak, last in the league in points scored, with the middle brother next on the schedule.

These two had split their history 1–1. Shmoody took the Week 1 opener in 2025, **160.08 to 130.56**. Abdo answered in Week 12, **129.18 to 102.86**. Then Shmoody went on to win the title while Abdo was knocked out in the quarterfinals. Week 6 was the rubber match, and the whole family was watching.
Little brother won it. Abdo beat Shmoody **118.64 to 113.34**. Oscar picked Shmoody 124–108, and Shmoody closed as an **11.5-point favorite**. Abdo now leads the all-time series **2–1**.

The win came from the players Abdo got from Tyler in their trade last Thursday. **DK Metcalf scored 20.30** and **George Pickens added 13.30**. **Jordan Love scored 20.24**, including a rushing touchdown, and **Dameon Pierce added 15.00** from the flex. Abdo won even with **Darren Waller scoring 0.00** at tight end and **Keenan Allen's 16.20** on his bench.

Shmoody had the bigger names. **James Cook ran for 24.30**, **Bryce Young delivered 19.84** and **Chris Boswell kicked 17.00**. His lineup choices cost him. **Cam Skattebo scored 0.00** in the flex while **Jakobi Meyers put up 13.30** on the bench. That swap alone would have won the game. The **Chiefs D/ST scored 15.00** on the bench while the Panthers D/ST he started managed 6.00. He left **47.60 points** on his bench in a game he lost by 5.30.

It's a painful pattern for the champion. Shmoody has lost to Hogies by **0.38**, to Collin by **5.42** and now to his little brother by **5.30**. He's 1–5, and three of those losses came by less than a touchdown.
Abdo is 2–4 and out of last place. Shmoody is 1–5 and will hear about this at every family meal. One score is still unsettled: Abdo against Mo is the rematch the family really wants.

body: Tyler taught Hogies this game: how to read a waiver wire, how to work a trade, how to sleep through a 1 p.m. kickoff without checking his phone. On Sunday, the student handed the teacher his worst score of the season.

The gap between them used to be enormous. In 2025 Tyler went **10–4**, scored **1,914.82 points** and reached the championship game before Shmoody beat him 173.30 to 107.30. Hogies went **6–8** and spent December in the toilet bowl, where he at least won the final and handed the trophy to Ryan. When they met in Week 11, the master won **144.80 to 94.02**.

That was last year. Hogies has started 2026 at **5–1**, and his only loss was a 162.88 to 156.30 shootout with Tyriese. Tyler came into Sunday on a three-game winning streak, fresh off ending Bob's perfect season and declaring a national holiday.

The holiday is over. Hogies won **134.32 to 88.52**, a **45.80-point** beating, and their all-time series is now **1–1**. Oscar picked Hogies 139–117. The line moved from Hogies −24.5 at the open to **−56** at kickoff, so the teacher technically covered. That is the only good news in this story.

Tyler's lineup was gutted before the game. **Six of his eight bench players were on bye**: Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown with Detroit, Aaron Jones, Jordan Mason and the Vikings D/ST with Minnesota, and Tee Higgins with Cincinnati. His whole bench scored **0.00**. He did remember his first lesson and traded for **Aaron Rodgers**, who covered Goff's bye with **16.02**. **Luther Burden led the team with 17.50** and **Jalen Coker added 15.70**, but **Juwan Johnson scored 0.00** at tight end and **Tyjae Spears managed 1.80** before Tyler cut him. **Bucky Irving**, Oscar's TD pick for Tyler, had already been traded to Abdo.

The student didn't need to do much. **Christian McCaffrey scored 30.70** with two touchdowns, **Chuba Hubbard added 19.10** and **Carnell Tate caught 19.00**. Hogies won by 45 with **Tyler Shough's 26.96 sitting on his bench** behind Dak Prescott's 11.02.

Hogies is tied with Sean for the league lead. Tyler is 3–3, still seventh, and holds the last playoff spot. Last December, Tyler played for a title while Hogies played for pride. This year, the student is at the front of the class.

These two have traded places in a hurry. Sean won the league's first championship in 2024, then crashed to **2–12** in 2025. That same year, Tyriese went **9–5** and reached the playoffs before Shmoody knocked him out. This preseason, everyone laughed at Tyriese's draft. Sean had his own drama. Last week he filed a missing person report for Kenneth Walker, who was simply on bye, and lost his perfect season to Shmoody. This week the case was solved. **Walker scored 27.90 with two touchdowns** and led Sean's team.

Sean won **145.28 to 113.78**, a **31.50-point** win that more than doubled the 15.5-point spread. body: Three brothers played three games in three weeks. Mo beat Baby Abdo in Week 5 and Abdo beat Shmoody in Week 6. On Sunday the oldest brother and the middle brother played the last game of the family round robin. The loser was going to do the dishes for good.

On Thursday it looked like Mo was the one heading for the sink. **Josh Allen was on bye** and he was the only quarterback on Mo's roster. The sportsbook believed his lineup: Shmoody opened at **−25**, and by Saturday the line had moved to **−43**, with the moneyline at **−1500**. Oscar picked Mo anyway, 117–113, "on the assumption that he finds a quarterback."
He found one. Overnight before Sunday's games, Mo claimed **Bo Nix off waivers for $0**. Nix threw for **26.28**, the best score of anyone in the game.

Mo won **133.68 to 117.82**. He was a 43-point underdog and won by **15.86**. Oscar's score of Mo 117 was close, and Oscar would like everyone to stop asking where he was on Thursday. **Rhamondre Stevenson ran for 22.50**. **Malik Nabers caught 18.10**. **Ollie Gordon**, the $133 waiver claim Mo won by two dollars over Marissa back in Week 3, added **17.30**. Ja'Marr Chase made it back into the lineup and scored **17.20**. Mo even left **Quinshon Judkins' 23.40** and **Tre Tucker's 21.30** on his bench.

Shmoody lost the game with his lineup choices again. On Friday night he picked up **Geno Smith** and then left him on the bench. Geno scored **23.48**. The quarterback Shmoody started, **Bryce Young**, scored **5.42**. That one swap would have won the game. **Cam Skattebo scored 19.10** on the bench while Tyler Allgeier managed 7.90 in the flex, and the **Panthers D/ST** finished at **−3.00**. Shmoody dropped them on Monday night. In total he left **61.58 points** on his bench.

His trades did their job. On Thursday Shmoody sent James Cook, who was on bye, to Tyler for **D'Andre Swift and Tee Higgins**. Swift scored **19.00** and Higgins **26.80**, which was 45.80 points from two players he'd owned for three days. It wasn't enough to make up for the quarterback decision.

Last year Shmoody won the title and Mo went 4–10. When they met in 2025, Shmoody won **117.44 to 79.30**. That series is now **1–1**. Mo went 0–4 to start the season and has now won three straight. He's sixth in the standings, his **977.44 points** are fourth in the league, and the sportsbook gives him an **83% playoff chance** and the fourth-best title odds (+495). Shmoody is 1–6 and in 11th, with a 4% chance of making the playoffs.

Maye's run of rushing touchdowns ended at three, which also cost Oscar a parlay leg. **Travis Kelce caught 4 for 72 and ran in a touchdown** (17.30), **Tetairoa McMillan caught a score** (15.60), and Cam Little kicked in 17.00. Saquon Barkley and Bhayshul Tuten each ran one in. She also started Adonai Mitchell, who scored 0.00, while Courtland Sutton's 15.50 sat on the bench. She won anyway.

Then it fell apart. **Mike Washington ran for −3 yards and scored −0.30.** Devin Singletary added 5.90, and Trey McBride was held to 12.40.

Marissa has won two straight and moves to **3–6**, and she's still on the road to the playoffs. Hogies' four-game winning streak is over. He's 7–2, and with Sean also at 7–2 with more points, **Hogies drops to the No. 2 seed.**

locker: Christian McCaffrey
Two touchdowns. Hogies sent me to Abdo and I sent Hogies to second place.
Oscar
Oscar picked Hogies and got the Tin Man. There's no place like first place, and as of Sunday, Hogies doesn't live there anymore.

body: Collin did what Collin does. He set up in spawn, planted his claymore, and stared in one direction waiting for Bob to walk into it. Bob came around the other side. The sportsbook opened Bob at −20 and closed him at −18.5, and he covered by 2.84. The fans were split 4–4. Oscar picked Bob 138–124 and said Collin would cover. He didn't, so Oscar got half of that one right.

Collin's claymore went off, but only once. **Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 74 yards and a touchdown** (13.40), cashing the golden leg of Oscar's parlay for a second straight week. **Justice Hill led the team with 18.20** and a touchdown of his own, and Jake Bates kicked in 15.00. Then came the friendly fire. **Kirk Cousins threw three interceptions** and finished with 12.64. **Jameson Williams scored 5.00 and Josh Downs 5.40**, so the two receivers from Collin's big trade night added up to 10.40. Braelon Allen fumbled. Collin's bench had nothing to send in either.

Bob ran his new quarterback right at him. **Brock Purdy threw for 232 yards and two touchdowns and ran in a third** for **25.28** in his first game for Bob, and **the 49ers D/ST added 21.00**. DeMario Douglas caught 5 for 102 (15.20). Bob won comfortably while his stars were quiet. **Jaxon Smith-Njigba was held to 12.10**, and Drake London caught 5 for 68 without the touchdown Oscar's parlay wanted. Bob also left **KC Concepcion's 18.80 and Denzel Boston's 15.80** on his bench. That's 34.60 points he didn't need.
Bob moves to **6–3** and gets back in the race for a bye. Collin's two-game winning streak is over. He's 4–5, still in the hunt, and still in spawn.
stories.headline: Look at this noob still in spawn: Sgt. Bob walks right past Collin's claymore
locker: Sgt. Bob
I knew exactly where the claymore was. Everybody does. He's been facing that same wall since Week 1.
Collin
I'm not camping. I'm holding a power position.
Oscar
Oscar said Collin would cover. Collin covered his spawn point instead.

body: The three-team trade rematch came down to **four hundredths of a point**. That's the **closest game in Villains history**, breaking the old record of 0.28 from Marissa's win over Sean in 2025. Shmoody also lost the second-closest, 0.38 to Hogies in Week 3. He's now been on the wrong end of the two closest games the league has ever seen.

The line flipped during the week. Tyriese opened as a 3-point favorite, but by Sunday, Shmoody was favored by 6.5. Tyriese won outright, and the game went over the 266.5 total. The fans liked Tyriese 7–1, and Oscar picked him 137–131. Oscar got the winner.

Shmoody led **126.32 to 118.66** going into Monday night. Each team had one player left in Bills at Vikings. Tyriese had **James Cook**. Shmoody had his kicker, **Will Reichard**. Cook **ran for 107 yards and a touchdown** for **16.70**. Reichard kicked for **9.00**. Tyriese needed 7.66 more than Shmoody on Monday night and got **7.70**.

He got there because of a quarterback decision. Tyriese benched Caleb Williams and started **C.J. Stroud**, who threw for **384 yards and five touchdowns** for **35.36**. Caleb scored 12.76 on the bench. **Tee Higgins**, traded away twice by Shmoody in five days, **caught two touchdowns for 20.20** in the revenge game, and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked in 17.00. It wasn't perfect: D'Andre Swift ran for 31 yards (3.10), and **Tank Dell scored 20.50 on the bench**.

Shmoody did everything but win. **Puka Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown** for **35.00**, the best game on the field. Bryce Young threw three touchdowns (20.34), and Nico Collins caught one (15.50). **Derrick Henry ran for 57 yards and somehow had −3 passing yards** for 5.58, missing his parlay leg. The bench hurt most of all. **Rome Odunze scored 16.00 and Quentin Johnston 13.30**, while Sam LaPorta (7.20) and Woody Marks (8.40) started. Either swap wins the game.
Tyriese wins his second straight and moves to **5–4**. Shmoody has lost four straight and is **1–8**. The champion's ship is sinking.
stories.headline: Pirate King! Tyriese steals the treasure by 0.04, the closest game in league history
locker: C.J. Stroud
Five touchdowns and Tyriese still needed a Monday night running back. That's how close this was.
Shmoody
Point zero four. I've been robbed by pirates twice this year.
Oscar
Oscar predicted arithmetic would beat nostalgia. He did not predict the arithmetic would come down to the second decimal.

body: On Friday, Abdo set his trap. He sent **Josh Jacobs and George Pickens to Hogies for Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black**. On Sunday, Tyler walked right into it. McCaffrey **scored two touchdowns for 22.70** in his first game for Abdo, and Abdo won by **54.68**. The sportsbook opened Tyler at −1.5 and moved him to −6. The fans liked Tyler 5–3, and Oscar picked him 129–126. Everyone was wrong except Abdo.

Abdo's whole deck came up. **Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and ran in a fourth** for **36.18**, the best quarterback game of the week. The babysitter finally got paid. **Bucky Irving ran for 97 yards and two touchdowns** (28.50). Bucky came from Tyler, as Oscar pointed out on Thursday, and he played like it. Omar Cooper caught 8 passes (13.80), and the Chiefs D/ST added 13.00. Abdo's **152.98 was the second-highest score of the week**. A.J. Brown didn't play, so Oscar's danger leg lived up to its name.

Tyler made his own move on Friday too. He traded **Brock Bowers and Javonte Williams to Sean for Jonathan Taylor and Jonah Coleman**. On Sunday, Bowers and Javonte scored **44.70 for Sean**. Taylor and Coleman scored **28.20 for Tyler**. Coleman ran one in (18.80), but **Taylor fumbled** and finished with 9.40. **Jared Goff threw for 170 yards and an interception** (5.30), **Zay Flowers caught 3 passes for 6 yards** (5.30), and **Ladd McConkey scored 0.00**. The highest scorer Tyler had left was a rookie running back.
Abdo moves to **4–5** and is back in the race. Tyler has lost four straight and is **3–6**, two games out of a playoff spot with five weeks left. His therapist has declined to comment.
stories.headline: You've activated my trap card! Baby Abdo sends Tyler to the Shadow Realm
locker: Jordan Love
Four touchdowns. The babysitter's done babysitting.
Tyler
I'll be back from the Shadow Realm. I'm already working on a trade.
Oscar
Oscar urged Tyler to put the whiteboard down. Instead he made another trade, and the trade card was the trap. Oscar has nothing further to add.

trades.headline: Tyler sells Jeremiyah Love for the Vikings backfield

sides.note: Tyler sent Jeremiyah Love (RB23, on injured reserve), Zonovan Knight (out) and $25 of FAAB to the Trade God for Aaron Jones Sr. (RB37) and Jordan Mason (RB41), the whole Vikings backfield. At 3–6 he needs backs who play on Sunday, and he got two. He paid with the most valuable piece in the deal, which is the usual price of urgency.

The Trade God takes on two injured backs, collects $25 for the trouble and comes out about 29% ahead. Love has the highest market value in the deal, and injured reserve is not forever. Patience is a virtue, particularly when someone else is paying for it.

Hogies sent Christian McCaffrey (RB4) and Kaelon Black to Baby Abdo for Josh Jacobs (RB16) and George Pickens (WR19), about 16% less value by the numbers. Sitting alone in first, he has chosen two starters over one star. Depth is what one calls it once the headliner has left.

Baby Abdo lands McCaffrey, still a top-five back, plus his handcuff Kaelon Black, and comes out about 16% ahead. He gives up two starters to do it, but stars win weeks and weeks win playoff spots. It is always pleasant to buy the best thing in the shop.

trades.headline: Tyler sends Bowers to Sean for Jonathan Taylor

sides.note: Tyler sent Brock Bowers (TE1) and Javonte Williams (RB8) to seanwavy for Jonathan Taylor (RB5) and rookie Jonah Coleman, about 25% less value, ten days after landing both in the three-team trade. Taylor has the highest market value in the deal, but the best tight end in the league is the harder thing to replace. One should never trade a rarity for a commodity, however handsome the commodity.

seanwavy adds the league's top tight end and a starting back and comes out about 25% ahead. He already scores more points than anyone in the league, and now he has the one position nobody else can fill. The rich, as ever, get Bowers.
Collin trades A.J. Brown (WR18) for Jameson Williams (WR26), who scored 14 points a game in Detroit before this. The cheaper of the two, which is not usually what one shops for.
Baby Abdo gets the bigger name and the bigger value. Brown has only 6.4 points a game in New England, so this is a bet on a reputation. Reputations, unlike receivers, rarely pull a hamstring.

One injury no longer wrecks his week, and when Mike Evans returns he will have one of the deepest benches in the league. Quantity has its own quality.

Collin sends DeVonta Smith (WR20, 17.2 a game) away for Josh Downs and $55 of FAAB. FAAB is lovely in December, but in October it does not score.
Tyriese adds a third WR1-type to his new depth chart for a bench piece and some loose change. Smith is questionable this week, which is the only fine print.
Collin turns a waiver-wire quarterback into $8 of free FAAB. Free money is the only kind that never disappoints.
Tyriese paid $8 for Kyler Murray and released him 25 seconds later. Whatever this was, it was not about Kyler.

FAAB counts at 0.04 value points per dollar. Trades made before the site launched were graded on Oct 14 with hindsight.

trades.headline: Tyler ships Nico Collins to Shmoody

sides.note: Tyler gave up the best player in the deal, Nico Collins (WR12), plus Blake Corum for Ladd McConkey (WR33) and Cam Skattebo (RB23). He traded one diamond for two lottery tickets, and Skattebo's 19.1 on Sunday suggests at least one of them may pay. A poor bargain, perhaps, but hardly a crime.

Shmoody takes the finest player in the deal, Nico Collins, plus Corum and his 17.1 points from Sunday, for two pieces he will scarcely miss. Winning a trade by 30 points of value is not a negotiation; it is a confession extracted politely.

trades.headline: Tyler flips Swift for James Cook

sides.note: Tyler kept D'Andre Swift for less than four hours before sending him and Tee Higgins (WR17) off for James Cook, the RB6, and Caleb Douglas. Cook is the finest player in the deal, but two good starters for one star and a passenger costs 14.5 points of value, and a man who trades that often is collecting receipts, not players.

Shmoody gave up James Cook, the RB6 with 47.1 points over the last two weeks, and was repaid on the spot: Swift scored 19 for him on Thursday night. Two reliable starters for one great one is the sort of arithmetic that wins matchups, if not admirers.

trades.headline: Tyler turns Amon-Ra into three starters

sides.note: Tyler parted with Amon-Ra St. Brown, the WR4, and came home with Zay Flowers (WR9), Nico Collins (WR12) and D'Andre Swift (RB12, 103.8 points), with Kyle Monangai for luggage. One diamond is a lovely thing to own; three good starters are a lovely thing to play, and Tyler has chosen the lineup over the jewellery box.

Zach kept Zay Flowers for barely twelve hours before cashing him, Nico Collins and D'Andre Swift in for Amon-Ra St. Brown, the WR4 and the finest player in the deal. Depth is a comfort, but stars win championships, and Zach has decided he would rather be brilliant than comfortable.

trades.headline: Zach flips Burrow for Zay Flowers

sides.note: seanwavy acquired Joe Burrow, one of only three quarterbacks this league deigns to value, but paid with Zay Flowers, the WR9 with 94.5 points to his name. DJ Moore has managed 36.3 points and Zach Charbonnet none at all; one should never exchange a reliable present for a merely interesting future.

Zach surrendered a premium quarterback and two hopes for Zay Flowers, the WR9, and Matthew Stafford, whose 111.86 points rather outshine Burrow's 104.24. To lose Joe Burrow looks like carelessness; to replace him with a cheaper man who has scored more looks suspiciously like wisdom.

trades.headline: Collin swaps Diggs for Kirk Cousins

sides.note: Collin gave up Stefon Diggs for Kirk Cousins, a quarterback in a league where quarterbacks are as plentiful as excuses. Cousins did score 18.52 on Sunday while Jameis Winston managed 6.48 for Collin, but one good afternoon on another man's bench is a flirtation, not a marriage.

Tyriese turned a bench quarterback into Stefon Diggs, a receiver with 53 points this season and two 15-plus weeks to his name. To lose a backup quarterback is a misfortune in most leagues; in this one it is merely housekeeping.

Zach let Kenny Gainwell go for $20 of waiver money, and money, however charming, has never scored a point on a Sunday. Still, Gainwell had spent three weeks on Zach's bench, so this was less a loss than a tidying of the wardrobe.

Marissa paid $20 for Kenny Gainwell, a modest back with 30.2 points this season and a projection of about nine a week. He went straight into her lineup and produced 3.4 — but one should never judge a purchase by its first outing, only by its price, and the price was low.

trades.headline: Tyler cashes in four for Amon-Ra

sides.note: Tyler sent four players out the door and came home with Amon-Ra St. Brown, the WR5 on the trade market with 104.2 points already, plus Jeremiyah Love and $10. One star is worth a crowd only if the crowd was mediocre; this crowd was a shade better, so the grade falls just short of the glamour.

Abdo gave up the brightest receiver in the deal for Bucky Irving (RB16), George Pickens (WR17), Jameson Williams and DK Metcalf. Quantity is the refuge of those who cannot afford quality, but with two flex spots to fill, Abdo can at least afford a full lineup.

trades.headline: Rodgers rides in for Goff’s bye

sides.note: Tyler, with Jared Goff on bye, bought Aaron Rodgers and was paid $18 to take him — a quarterback projected for 15.9 this week is a fine thing to borrow. But Brian Robinson was worth a shade more, and in this league a spare quarterback is the one luxury everyone already owns.

Collin parted with a quarterback and $18 for Brian Robinson, a running back with 50.1 points to his name. To give away what is easily replaced and receive what is not is the whole art of commerce, even when the receipt is modest.
Tyler sold Kaelon Black for $20 of FAAB. Small stakes, small grade.
Hogies spent $20 on a handcuff for Christian McCaffrey. Insurance is boring until the house burns down.
Tyler sent Breece Hall back where he came from and came away with three contributors. Aaron Jones put up 18.7 in the Week 5 win over Bob.
Collin got Breece Hall back, which is either a correction or an admission. Braelon Allen gave him 18.6 in Week 5.
Marissa paid $100 of FAAB and a starting quarterback to get a different starting quarterback. In this league that is like buying sand at the beach.
In a one-quarterback league, quarterbacks are cheap, and Tim knew it. He moved Mahomes, kept a starter in Bo Nix and pocketed $100 of FAAB for the trouble.
Tyler reacquired Marvin Harrison, who has since been traded to Houston, and added Braelon Allen for RJ Harvey. Two for one is a decent afternoon.
Baby Abdo consolidated two pieces into RJ Harvey, a reasonable flex play. The value went slightly the other way.
Collin gave up a receiver for a quarterback in a league where quarterbacks grow on trees. Herbert has since left his roster, which rather proves the point.
Jakobi Meyers is only a bench piece, but Shmoody turned a replaceable quarterback into a receiver who can fill a flex spot. A quiet win.
Two starters for Alvin Kamara. Collin finally won a trade, and he won it cleanly.
Bob traded two players for Alvin Kamara, who produced 2.6 points in Week 5. The General’s intelligence services have failed him.

trades.headline: Jefferson and Warren for Bucky and Pickens

sides.note: On paper Mo got the bigger names. On the field, Bucky Irving and George Pickens combined for 59.5 points in Week 5 and powered the win over Bob. The grade says C; the scoreboard disagrees.
Mo collected Justin Jefferson and Jaylen Warren, and Warren’s 36.8 helped set the league record. Jefferson’s bye this week is the only blemish.
Tee Higgins and Jalen Coker are fine receivers. Zay Flowers is a better one, and Tyler gave him up along with a running back.
Zay Flowers has become a top-ten receiver on the market. Sean keeps beating Tyler in trades; perhaps he should start charging admission.

Collin sent away Lamar Jackson, one of the three quarterbacks in this league actually worth paying for, but came back with three useful bodies in Hurts, Diggs and Bateman. Depth is a consolation prize, though not a worthless one.
Baby Abdo landed Lamar Jackson, one of the league's rare quarterbacks who changes a week on his own, plus Marvin Harrison before his move to Houston. Lamar carries this grade by himself.
George Kittle for Devaughn Vele is the kind of trade that earns a man the name Trade God. Kittle is a top-three tight end by market value.
The defending champion swapped an elite tight end for a backup receiver. Some champions defend their crown; Shmoody appears to have pawned it.
Breece Hall was the prize, and Tyler turned three pieces into a starting running back and a receiver. Quality over quantity, for once.
Collin took the volume, but Harrison and Kamara were both traded on within a week. DeVonta Smith is the only piece still standing.
Days after acquiring Kenneth Walker, Tyler sent him back to Sean for three depth pieces. Walker has since become one of the most valuable players in the league. Oscar has no further questions.
Sean lost Walker, then got him back with Kyler Murray attached. The rare trade where the victim of the first robbery writes the sequel.
Tyler swapped one ordinary quarterback for another and collected $30 of FAAB for his trouble. In this league that's a fair deal.
Zach paid $30 to swap Kyler Murray for Jayden Daniels, two quarterbacks this league treats as interchangeable. No harm done, and little gained.
Tyler surrendered Josh Allen, now the top quarterback in fantasy, for Jayden Daniels and Marvin Harrison, who has since been traded to Houston. Ten FAAB dollars do not buy forgiveness.
Mo walked away with Josh Allen, who threw for 30.5 points in the record-breaking 196-point week. Jonathon Brooks was a lottery ticket; Allen was the jackpot.
Two useful receivers out the door for a rookie running back who gave the Trade God 4.8 points in Week 5. Even gods have off days.
Denzel Boston has turned into a weekly starter and Deebo Samuel adds depth. The General recruited two soldiers for the price of one.

trades.headline: Walker for Lamb, and Tyler wins the swap

sides.note: Kenneth Walker is now the fourth-most valuable player in fantasy, and Tyler got Jameson Williams thrown in. A splendid piece of business, undone only by what Tyler did next.
CeeDee Lamb is a fine receiver, but giving up a top-five running back for him looks worse every week. Tyjae Spears does not change the arithmetic.
